docs.title: kuke connector
docs.text:
List connectors and their identities, import your git identity from this host, and set the default identity a Realm gives its cells.

kuke connector list
kuke connector import git [--key PATH] [--passphrase-file FILE] [--known-hosts FILE]
                          [--hosts HOST[,HOST...]] [--name NAME] [--realm REALM]
                          [--default] [--dry-run]
kuke connector default <connector> [<identity>[@realm[/space[/stack]]]]
                       [--realm REALM] [--method METHOD] [--clear]

A connector is a kind of access a cell needs — a harness login, an API token, a git identity, a registry credential. Its identities are Secrets tagged with the connector, and a Realm, Space or Stack default names the identity every cell in it uses.

Every subcommand talks to kukeond and honours --host / KUKEON_HOST. No subcommand prints secret material.

docs.title: Subcommands
docs.text: Command What it does kuke connector list Print each connector's identities and each Realm's default identity kuke connector import git Store your SSH key and global gitconfig author as one git identity kuke connector default Set or clear a Realm's default identity for a connector

docs.title: kuke connector list
docs.text:
kuke connector list

Prints two tables. IDENTITIES has one row per Secret tagged with a connector; a connector with no identity gets a row of dashes. REALM DEFAULTS has one row per Realm default, the identity written name@realm[/space[/stack]]. The command reads Secret metadata only, never the material.

$ kuke connector list
IDENTITIES
CONNECTOR  IDENTITY     SCOPE    TYPE
---------  -----------  -------  -------
claude     -            -        -
codex      -            -        -
git        git-ssh      default  ssh-key
github     work-github  default  opaque
registry   -            -        -

REALM DEFAULTS
CONNECTOR  METHOD  REALM    IDENTITY
---------  ------  -------  -------------------
git        -       default  git-ssh@default
github     token   default  work-github@default

With no default set, the second table reads No realm sets a default identity.

docs.title: kuke connector import git
docs.text:
kuke connector import git [flags]

Discovers the SSH key and the global git configuration of the user running the command and stores them as one Secret tagged git. Run it as your own account, not under sudo, which can read root's home directory and git configuration instead. The Home: line of --dry-run shows which home is read.

Flag Default Description --key — Private key to import. Default: the key user.signingkey names, else ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, id_ecdsa, id_rsa. --passphrase-file — File holding the key's passphrase. Required for an encrypted key. --known-hosts — known_hosts file pinning host keys. Default: the built-in keys of github.com, gitlab.com, bitbucket.org. --hosts github.com Hosts or URL prefixes the key authenticates. Comma-separated or repeated. --name git-ssh Name of the identity Secret. git-author for an author-only identity. --realm default Realm the Secrets are stored in. --default false Also make the identity the Realm's default git identity, replacing any existing one. --dry-run false Print what discovery found. Store nothing and make no daemon call.

docs.title: With an SSH key
docs.text:
The import stores an ssh-key Secret (default name git-ssh) with these identity fields:

Field Value author user.name <user.email> from the global git configuration committer the same hosts --hosts, default github.com sign commits for commit.gpgsign, tags for tag.gpgsign — only when user.signingkey is this key allowedSignersRef git-allowed-signers, when gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile is set

The public key (<key>.pub) and the certificate (<key>-cert.pub) next to the key are stored too.

Signing is imported only when user.signingkey names the imported key — its path, its .pub file, or the public key itself. A GPG key or a different SSH key does not turn on signing, and a note says so: a cell signing with a key your forge does not know as your signing key would produce unverified commits. To sign, rerun with --key naming the signing key.

When gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile is set, the file is stored as the opaque Secret git-allowed-signers in the same realm, and the identity names it.

An explicit --key that does not exist, a key that cannot be read, or a passphrase-protected key without --passphrase-file is an error.

docs.title: Without a key
docs.text:
When no key is found and --key is not given, the import stores an opaque author-only identity named git-author and says so. Cells that use it get the author and committer, and no credential and no signing. --hosts, --passphrase-file and --known-hosts are ignored, each with a note.

With neither a key nor a git author the import fails:

import git identity: no SSH private key under /home/me/.ssh (name one with --key) and no git author (set user.name and user.email in the global git configuration)

docs.title: Rerunning
docs.text: Rerunning the import updates the Secrets in place: same name, same realm, new content.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
$ kuke connector import git
Secret "git-allowed-signers" (realm "default"): created
Secret "git-ssh" (realm "default"): created
Git identity git-ssh@default (ssh-key for github.com, author Ada Lovelace <ada@example.com>, signs commits,tags)
Make it the default with: kuke connector default git git-ssh@default

Notes follow as Note: … lines. With --default the last line reports the Realm default it set and the one it replaced:

Realm "default" default git identity: git-ssh@default (was none)
Realm "default" default git identity: git-ssh@default (replaces other@default)

docs.title: Dry run
docs.text:
$ kuke connector import git --dry-run
Dry run: nothing is stored.
Home: /home/me
Secret: git-ssh@default (type ssh-key, connector git)
Key: /home/me/.ssh/id_ed25519
Allowed signers: /home/me/.ssh/allowed_signers (secret git-allowed-signers@default)
Identity:
  allowedSignersRef: git-allowed-signers
  author: Ada Lovelace <ada@example.com>
  committer: Ada Lovelace <ada@example.com>
  hosts: github.com
  sign: commits,tags

An author-only import prints Key: none (author-only identity). With --default the dry run also prints the default it would set. Key material is never printed.

docs.title: kuke connector default
docs.text:
kuke connector default <connector> [<identity>[@realm[/space[/stack]]]] [flags]

Sets the identity a Realm gives every Config in it that chooses none — the same change as the default picker on the web UI's Connectors page (POST /api/connectors/{connector}/defaults). The Secret must exist and be an identity of the connector.

Flag Default Description --realm the identity's realm, else default Realm whose default is set. --method — Method the default is for, for a connector with several. --clear false Remove the Realm's default. Takes no identity.

An identity without a realm is looked up in --realm, else default. A connector with several methods that take an identity (claude: subscription and api-key) needs --method. The command prints the new default and the one it replaced, in the same form as import git --default.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Make git-ssh@default the default git identity of realm default
kuke connector default git git-ssh

# Realm dev, identity git-ssh@dev
kuke connector default git git-ssh --realm dev

# A token default for one method of a multi-method connector
kuke connector default claude claude-team --method subscription

# Remove the default
kuke connector default git --clear

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Connectors — the git connector and author-only identities
  • Git credentials and identity — the guide built around import git
  • kuke create secret --connector — create an identity by hand

docs.title: kuke create
docs.text:
Imperative creation of a single resource. For anything more than a one-off, prefer kuke apply against a manifest.

kuke create <resource> [NAME] [flags]
kuke c      <resource> [NAME] [flags]      # alias

Resources: realm, space, stack, cell, blueprint, config, secret, registry-credential. Each subcommand also has a short alias (r, sp, st, ce, bp, cfg, secret has none, and registry-credential has registry-cred/regcred).

docs.title: kuke create realm
docs.text:
kuke create realm [NAME] [--namespace <ns>]
Flag Default Description --namespace <realm>.kukeon.io (derived) Containerd namespace for the realm 
sudo kuke create realm mytenant
sudo kuke create realm mytenant --namespace mytenant.kukeon.io

docs.title: kuke create space
docs.text:
kuke create space [NAME] --realm <realm>
Flag Default Description --realm default Realm that will own the space 
sudo kuke create space blog --realm default

docs.title: kuke create stack
docs.text:
kuke create stack [NAME] --realm <realm> --space <space>
Flag Default Description --realm default Realm that owns the stack --space default Space that owns the stack 
sudo kuke create stack wordpress --realm default --space blog

docs.title: kuke create cell
docs.text:
kuke create cell [NAME] --realm <r> --space <s> --stack <t>
                       ( --image <ref> [--command <cmd>]
                       | --from-blueprint <bp> [--param K=V]... [--param-file <path>]
                       | --from-config <cfg> [--env K=V]... [--connector C=SECRET]... [--connector-method C=METHOD]... [--dry-run [--explain]]
                       | --clone <cell> [--param K=V]... [--env K=V]... )

Four source modes (exactly one of --image / --from-blueprint / --from-config / --clone is required):

  • kuke create cell [name] --image <ref> [--command <cmd>] — synthesizes a single attachable container from a bare image ref and persists it in a stopped state (the quick-start source, the create-side mirror of kuke run --image). Pair with kuke start <name>. --command overrides the synthesized entrypoint (default /bin/sh). No daemon-stored binding is resolved, so the binding render-time/override knobs --param/--param-file/--env are rejected with --image (use --from-blueprint/--from-config to parameterise or layer env). Mutually exclusive with --from-blueprint/--from-config/--clone.
  • kuke create cell [name] --from-blueprint <bp> [--param K=V]... [--param-file <path>] — resolves the daemon-stored CellBlueprint, applies scalar params, materialises the full Cell record (containers and all), and persists it in a stopped state. Pair with kuke start <name>. Differs from kuke run --from-blueprint (materialise + start + attach) by leaving the cell stopped for inspection or hand-off; Blueprint-lineage cells reach the recreate branch of kuke restart's daemon-side reconcile (P7) — updates flow through restart, not in-place mutation.
  • kuke create cell [name] --from-config <cfg> [--mode <m>] [--param K=V]... [--env K=V]... [--dry-run [--explain]] — kukeond renders the cell from the daemon-stored CellConfig and its referenced Blueprint — merging the Realm → Space → Stack spec.defaults under the Config's spec.values + repo/secret slot fills, deeper levels winning per key (see Defaults merge) — and persists it in stopped state. --dry-run prints the rendered Cell without creating it; --explain prints every merged value with the level that set it — including the enabled components, the picked mode, the required image capabilities and the git identity and credential each repo uses — and the rendered cell's digest. --mode picks the harness mode the cell is created in (default: the Config's); --param is accepted only for that mode's parameters. Pair with kuke start <name>. Later reconcile against the lineage Config flows through kuke restart <name> (OutOfSync-driven, #821) once the cell is started.
  • kuke create cell [name] --clone <cell> [--param K=V]... | [--env K=V]... — forks an existing cell's recipe: reads the source cell's Spec.Provenance (the Blueprint/Config binding it was materialised from plus any recorded per-cell overrides) and re-materialises from that same binding. The clone copies the source's provenance verbatim, inherits its kukeon.io/config / kukeon.io/blueprint lineage label, and is stamped with a kukeon.io/source-cell=<src> annotation. Additional --param (Blueprint-lineage source) or --env (Config-lineage source) stack on top of the source's recorded overrides, last-write-wins; the per-source symmetry below applies to the stacked overrides. A source cell with no provenance (a hand-built cell never materialised from a binding) cannot be cloned.

Cell name (unified <prefix>-<6hex> rule). NAME is optional. When omitted, the cell name is generated: <prefix>-<6hex> for --from-blueprint/--from-config (prefix = the blueprint's spec.prefix, defaulting to its metadata.name), <source-name>-<6hex> for --clone, and <image-short-name>-<6hex> for --image (e.g. docker.io/library/alpine:3 → alpine-<6hex>). An explicit NAME is used verbatim. The Config / Blueprint name is not the cell name — it survives only as the kukeon.io/{config,blueprint} lineage label (epic:cell-identity).

--connector (per-cell identity). --connector <connector>=<secret>[@realm[/space[/stack]]] uses another stored identity for one connector of this cell — for example --connector github=other-github. It is valid with --from-config only and repeatable, once per connector; --clone of such a cell carries the source's overrides over unchanged. A secret named without a scope is looked up in the cell's realm. The override wins over the Config's fill and every Realm/Space/Stack default, is recorded in Spec.Provenance.connectorOverrides, and so survives kuke restart and a reconcile-driven recreate. A connector the Config does not require, a missing Secret, or a Secret tagged for another connector or of a type the connector does not accept is rejected. A Config whose required connector resolves to no identity cannot be previewed or created: the error names the connector.

--connector-method (per-cell method). --connector-method <connector>=<method> uses another method of a connector for this cell — for example --connector-method codex=api-key on a Config that uses login. The blueprint component of that method is enabled in place of the one the Config enables; the method's identity then resolves through --connector, the Config and the Realm/Space/Stack defaults. Valid with --from-config only and repeatable, once per connector; recorded in Spec.Provenance.connectorMethods, so it survives kuke restart, a reconcile-driven recreate and --clone. A connector the Config's blueprint declares no methods for, a method it does not declare, or a connector the Config does not require (a method pick swaps a method, it never adds a connector) is rejected.

--param / --env symmetry. Blueprints take render-time --param; Configs take persisted per-cell --env. --param/--param-file are valid with --from-blueprint and rejected with --from-config (a Config carries its own spec.values — edit the Config instead); symmetrically, --env KEY=VALUE is valid with --from-config (a per-cell override layered on the Config's resolved values, baked into the CellDoc and recorded in Spec.Provenance.envOverrides) and rejected with --from-blueprint. On --clone, the source's lineage decides which applies: --param on a Blueprint-lineage source, --env on a Config-lineage source. The same cell.ValidateOverrideSymmetry gate enforces this on kuke run and kuke create cell alike.

Flag Default Description [NAME] (positional) (generated) The cell name. Optional: omitted → generated <prefix>-<6hex> (<source-name>-<6hex> with --clone); explicit name used verbatim --realm default Realm that owns the cell --space default Space that owns the cell --stack default Stack that owns the cell --image "" Image ref to synthesize a single attachable container from. A fourth source; mutually exclusive with --from-blueprint/--from-config/--clone. Rejects --param/--param-file/--env --command "" With --image: override the synthesized container's entrypoint (default /bin/sh). Only valid with --image --from-blueprint "" Daemon-stored CellBlueprint name. Exactly one of --image/--from-blueprint/--from-config/--clone is required; the four are mutually exclusive --from-config "" Daemon-stored CellConfig name. Exactly one of --image/--from-blueprint/--from-config/--clone is required; the four are mutually exclusive --clone "" Existing cell to fork. Re-materialises from the source's provenance binding, copies its provenance, inherits its lineage label, stamps kukeon.io/source-cell=<src> --param (empty, repeatable) Scalar parameter override KEY=VALUE. Valid with --from-blueprint (and a Blueprint-lineage --clone); rejected with --from-config (a Config carries its own spec.values) --param-file "" File of KEY=VALUE lines seeding scalar parameters. Same declaration rules as --param; --param wins on dups. Rejected with --from-config --env (empty, repeatable) Persisted per-cell override KEY=VALUE. Valid with --from-config (and a Config-lineage --clone); baked into the CellDoc + Spec.Provenance.envOverrides. Rejected with --from-blueprint --connector (empty, repeatable) Per-cell identity override CONNECTOR=SECRET[@realm[/space[/stack]]]. Valid with --from-config only; recorded in Spec.Provenance.connectorOverrides --connector-method (empty, repeatable) Per-cell method CONNECTOR=METHOD: enable that method's component instead of the Config's. Valid with --from-config only; recorded in Spec.Provenance.connectorMethods --dry-run false With --from-config: ask kukeond to render the cell and print it without creating anything. Rejected with other sources --explain false With --from-config: print every merged value with its origin (realm, space, stack, config, blueprint) and the render digest 
# Synthesize a single-container cell from an image, stopped (the quick-start path)
sudo kuke create cell my-first --image docker.io/library/alpine:3
sudo kuke start my-first

# Materialise from Blueprint, stopped (generated name web-template-<6hex>)
sudo kuke create cell --from-blueprint web-template --param IMAGE=nginx:1.27 \
    --realm default --space blog --stack wordpress

# Same, pin the cell name "web"
sudo kuke create cell web --from-blueprint web-template --param IMAGE=nginx:1.27 \
    --realm default --space blog --stack wordpress
sudo kuke start web --realm default --space blog --stack wordpress

# Materialise from Config, stopped, with a persisted per-cell env override
sudo kuke create cell prod --from-config prod-config --env LOG_LEVEL=debug \
    --realm default --space blog --stack wordpress
sudo kuke start prod --realm default --space blog --stack wordpress

# Preview the daemon-side render and where each merged value came from
sudo kuke create cell prod --from-config prod-config --dry-run --explain \
    --realm default --space blog --stack wordpress

# Fork an existing cell's recipe into a sibling (generated name prod-<6hex>)
sudo kuke create cell --clone prod \
    --realm default --space blog --stack wordpress

docs.title: kuke create blueprint
docs.text:
kuke create blueprint [NAME] [--realm <r>] [--space <s>] [--stack <t>]

Scaffold a kind: CellBlueprint starter YAML to stdout. Emits a syntactically-valid Blueprint document with a single placeholder container, the operator's --realm/--space/--stack as scope, and inline # TODO markers on the required image: field plus comment markers for optional sections (parameters, ports, volumes, repos, secrets) so operators know what they can add.

No daemon call — pure stdout emission.

Flag Default Description <NAME> (positional) (required) The blueprint name --realm default Realm that owns the blueprint --space default Space that owns the blueprint --stack default Stack that owns the blueprint 
kuke create blueprint web > web.yaml
$EDITOR web.yaml          # fill image, add parameters/repos/secrets/...
sudo kuke apply -f web.yaml

docs.title: kuke create config
docs.text:
kuke create config [NAME] --from-blueprint <bp> [--realm <r>] [--space <s>] [--stack <t>]

Scaffold a kind: CellConfig YAML from a CellBlueprint. Reads the referenced Blueprint from the daemon, introspects its declared scalar parameters and structural repo/secret slots, and emits a starter Config YAML to stdout with defaults pre-filled and # TODO markers where the operator must fill required-no-default parameters and slot sources. The output is not written to the daemon — pipe it to kuke apply -f - after editing.

Flag Default Description <NAME> (positional) (required) The config name --from-blueprint (required) Source CellBlueprint name --realm default Realm that owns the config (also the default Blueprint lookup scope) --space default Space that owns the config (also the default Blueprint lookup scope) --stack default Stack that owns the config (also the default Blueprint lookup scope) 
kuke create config prod --from-blueprint web > prod-config.yaml
$EDITOR prod-config.yaml  # fill required slot sources, override defaults
sudo kuke apply -f prod-config.yaml
sudo kuke run --from-config prod   # stamp + start + attach a fresh cell from the Config

docs.title: kuke create secret
docs.text:
kuke create secret [NAME] [--type opaque|basic-auth|ssh-key] <source flags>
                          [--connector <c> [--identity FIELD=VALUE]... [--<field> <value>]...]
                          [--realm <r>] [--space <s>] [--stack <t>]

Create a kind: Secret within a scope. --type selects what it holds (Secret manifest); every value is write-only.

--type opaque (default) — an arbitrary value, referenceable via ContainerSecret.secretRef from a CellConfig's slot fill:

  • kuke create secret <name> --from-literal=KEY=VAL — inline value, repeatable. Multiple values are joined by newline.
  • kuke create secret <name> --from-file=<path> — read value from file.

At least one of --from-literal or --from-file is required.

--type basic-auth — a git credential for HTTPS remotes: --username plus exactly one of --password-stdin, --token-stdin, --from-file (password file) or --token-file.

--type ssh-key — a git credential and signing key for SSH: --from-file <private key>, plus the optional passphrase, public key, certificate and pinned host keys.

The two git types are used through a git block — see the git credentials guide — and cannot be consumed as a container secrets[] entry. A flag that belongs to another type is rejected.

--connector <name> tags the secret as an identity of a connector, so it can be picked by name for a team, a Config or one cell. The secret is validated against the connector: its type must be one the connector accepts (when --type is omitted and the connector accepts exactly one type, that type is used), required identity fields must be set, and each value must read as its declared type. The connector's readable identity fields are set with --identity FIELD=VALUE (repeatable) or with the flag of the same name — every field of every connector in the catalog is a flag, in kebab case (--author, --hosts, --allowed-signers-ref, …). kuke create secret --help lists the connectors and the field flags. An unknown connector, an unknown field, or a field given without --connector is rejected.

The git connector accepts ssh-key, basic-auth and opaque. An opaque git identity is author-only: it requires --author, stores no value and takes no --hosts, --sign or --allowed-signers-ref. --connector git without --type and without --from-file creates one; with --from-file, --type is required. --from-literal or --from-file on an author-only identity fails with an author-only git identity stores no value; use --type ssh-key for a key. To store your own key and author in one step, use kuke connector import git.

Flag Type Default Description <NAME> (positional) all (required) The secret name --realm all default Realm that owns the secret --space all (realm-scoped) Space that owns the secret --stack all (realm-scoped) Stack that owns the secret (requires --space) --type all opaque opaque, basic-auth or ssh-key --from-literal opaque (empty, repeatable) Specify a key-value pair as KEY=VAL --from-file all "" opaque: the value. basic-auth: the password. ssh-key: the private key --username basic-auth "" The HTTP user --password-stdin basic-auth false Read the password from stdin --token-stdin basic-auth false Read a token from stdin --token-file basic-auth "" Read a token from a file --passphrase-stdin ssh-key false Read the private key's passphrase from stdin --passphrase-file ssh-key "" Read the private key's passphrase from a file --public-key-file ssh-key "" The matching public key --certificate-file ssh-key "" An OpenSSH user certificate for the key --known-hosts-file ssh-key "" Pinned host keys in known_hosts format --connector all "" Connector the secret is an identity of --identity all (empty, repeatable) A readable identity field of the connector, FIELD=VALUE --<field> all "" One flag per identity field of the catalog (--author, --hosts, …) 
# Inline value
sudo kuke create secret api-key --from-literal=API_KEY=sk-... --realm default

# From file
sudo kuke create secret tls-cert --from-file=./tls.crt --realm default

# SSH key for git (clone, push, signing)
sudo kuke create secret git-ssh --type ssh-key --from-file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 --realm default

# Passphrase-protected key with a certificate and pinned host keys
sudo kuke create secret git-ssh --type ssh-key --from-file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 \
    --passphrase-file ./passphrase --certificate-file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519-cert.pub \
    --known-hosts-file ./forge_known_hosts --realm default

# HTTPS username + token
printf %s "$TOKEN" | sudo kuke create secret forge-https --type basic-auth \
    --username dev-bot --token-stdin --realm default

# An identity of the github connector
sudo kuke create secret work-github --connector github --from-file ./token

# A git identity: the key plus its readable facts
sudo kuke create secret bot-key --connector git --type ssh-key --from-file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 \
    --author 'Dev Bot <bot@example.com>' --hosts github.com --sign commits,tags

# An author-only git identity: no key, no value
sudo kuke create secret me --connector git --author 'Me <me@example.com>'

kuke get secrets lists each secret's TYPE and CONNECTOR (-o wide adds its readable IDENTITY fields); no verb prints a value.

docs.title: kuke create registry-credential
docs.text:
kuke create registry-credential <realm> --username <u> (--password-stdin | --from-file <path>)
                                         [--server <host>] [--secret-name <name>]

Attach private-registry pull credentials to an existing realm. The command stores the username and token as a basic-auth Secret of the realm — an identity of the registry connector — upserts an entry onto the realm's spec.registryCredentials that names the Secret, keyed by --server, and re-applies the realm. The realm document never carries the token. The reconciler converges the change as a compatible update — no realm recreate and no cell disruption — so cells in the realm can immediately pull images that previously returned 403 Forbidden.

Re-running with the same --server rotates the Secret and updates that entry in place rather than appending a duplicate; a different --server appends a new entry. Existing entries for other servers are preserved. An entry for the server that still carries an inline username and password is replaced by the Secret-backed one, which is how an existing inline password moves into a Secret.

The token never enters argv: supply it via --password-stdin (read from stdin, docker-login style) or --from-file (read from a file). Exactly one of the two is required.

Flag Default Description <realm> (positional) (required) The realm to attach the credential to --username (required) Registry username --password-stdin false Read the registry token from stdin --from-file "" Read the registry token from a file --server "" (matches image's host) Registry host the credential applies to (e.g. ghcr.io); empty matches the registry extracted from the image reference at pull time --secret-name registry-<server> Name of the Secret that stores the credential (ghcr.io → registry-ghcr-io; an empty --server → registry-default) 
# Pipe a token in from stdin (no token in shell history)
echo "$GHCR_TOKEN" | sudo kuke create registry-credential default \
    --server ghcr.io --username my-user --password-stdin

# Or read it from a file
sudo kuke create registry-credential default \
    --server ghcr.io --username my-user --from-file ./ghcr-token.txt

docs.title: Imperative vs. declarative
docs.text: kuke create is useful for quick experiments and one-off resources. For anything you want to commit, diff, or apply repeatedly, write a YAML manifest and use kuke apply. Manifests are the unit of version control; imperative commands are not.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• kuke apply — declarative alternative
  • kuke run — create + start a single cell in one shot
  • Manifest Reference — the schema for each resource

docs.title: kuke daemon
docs.text:
Manage the kukeond daemon cell lifecycle.

kuke daemon [command]

These commands act on the kukeond cell provisioned by kuke init (kuke-system / kukeon / kukeon / kukeond). They run in-process because the daemon they manage may not be running at the time the command is invoked.

docs.title: Subcommands
docs.text:
Command What it does kuke daemon start Start the kukeond daemon cell kuke daemon stop Gracefully stop the kukeond cell (SIGTERM, escalating to SIGKILL) kuke daemon kill Immediately SIGKILL the kukeond daemon cell kuke daemon restart Stop then start the kukeond daemon cell kuke daemon reset Stop, delete metadata + cgroups, clear /run/kukeon/kukeond.{sock,pid} kuke daemon recreate Recreate the kukeond daemon cell (tear down, re-provision, start) kuke daemon logs Print the kukeond daemon's stdout/stderr (use -f to follow)

All subcommands are idempotent: they succeed with a clear message when the daemon is already in the requested state.

docs.title: Targeting a specific instance
docs.text:
Every kuke daemon … subcommand accepts --server-configuration <path> (default /etc/kukeon/kukeond.yaml) to point at a non-default kukeond instance. The precedence chain matches kuke init and kuke uninstall:

  1. --server-configuration <path> (flag)
  2. KUKEOND_CONFIGURATION environment variable
  3. /etc/kukeon/kukeond.yaml (default file)
  4. Hardcoded defaults (absent file)

The same chain kukeond itself uses, so a --server-configuration ./kukeond-dev.yaml on any admin command points at the same document the daemon honors. Running sudo kuke daemon stop --server-configuration ./kukeond-dev.yaml signals the dev instance only; the prod kukeond (under the default /etc/kukeon/kukeond.yaml) is untouched.

docs.title: kuke daemon start
docs.text: Bring up the existing kukeond cell provisioned by kuke init. Returns success when the daemon is already running. Errors when the host has not been initialized — run kuke init first.

docs.title: kuke daemon stop
docs.text:
Send SIGTERM and wait up to --timeout (default 10s) for the daemon to exit; if the grace period expires, escalate to SIGKILL.

Flag Default Description --timeout 10s Grace period before escalating from SIGTERM to SIGKILL

docs.title: kuke daemon kill
docs.text: Force-kill the kukeond cell with no grace period. This is the escape hatch for a hung or unresponsive daemon — use kuke daemon stop for the graceful path.

docs.title: kuke daemon restart
docs.text:
Compose kuke daemon stop and kuke daemon start into a single verb. When the daemon is already stopped, the stop phase is skipped and the start phase still runs.

Flag Default Description --timeout 10s Grace period for the stop phase before escalating from SIGTERM to SIGKILL

docs.title: kuke daemon recreate
docs.text:
sudo kuke daemon recreate --kukeond-image <image> [--timeout <duration>] [--server-configuration <path>]

Recreate the kukeond daemon cell (tear down, re-provision, start).

Compose kuke daemon reset and kuke init's kukeond cell provisioning into a single verb.

Tears down the existing kukeond cell (stop, delete, clear socket+pid) and re-provisions it from scratch using the specified --kukeond-image. The cell-creation path is shared with kuke init, so the two cannot drift.

Requires --kukeond-image and errors with ErrHostNotInitialized when the host has not been bootstrapped by kuke init yet.

Image-load is out of scope: the desired image must already be present in the kuke-system realm (via kuke build or kuke image load) before invoking this command.

Flag Default Description --kukeond-image (required) Container image for kukeond. May be omitted if kukeondImage is set in /etc/kukeon/kukeond.yaml; otherwise required. --timeout 10s (lifecycle.DefaultTimeout) Grace period for the stop phase before escalating from SIGTERM to SIGKILL --server-configuration /etc/kukeon/kukeond.yaml Path to the kukeond server-configuration YAML (precedence chain: flag > KUKEOND_CONFIGURATION env > default file > hardcoded defaults)

docs.title: kuke daemon reset
docs.text:
Lightweight dev-loop teardown of the kukeond daemon. Stops the cell (with the same SIGTERM → SIGKILL escalation as daemon stop), deletes the cell metadata + cgroups, and clears the transient files /run/kukeon/kukeond.{sock,pid}. User-realm data under /opt/kukeon/default/** is left intact, so re-running kuke init after kuke daemon reset produces a clean re-bootstrap.

Always runs as root: it touches /sys/fs/cgroup, containerd namespaces, and /opt/kukeon. Fails fast with a clear remediation if you forget sudo.

Distinct from kuke uninstall, which is the per-host teardown (every realm, the kukeon system user/group, and the run path itself).

Flag Default Description --purge-system false Also remove /opt/kukeon/kuke-system (user-realm data is still preserved) --timeout 10s Grace period for the stop phase before escalating from SIGTERM to SIGKILL

docs.title: kuke daemon logs
docs.text:
Print the kukeond container's stdout/stderr stream. Shortcut for kuke log --realm kuke-system --space kukeon --stack kukeon kukeond — the coordinates are static and filled in for you.

kuke daemon logs [-f]
kuke daemon log  [-f]      # alias

By default the current contents are printed and the command exits; pass -f/--follow to tail until SIGINT.

The command reads through kukeond's read-only ReadDaemonLogs socket method (at KUKEON_HOST) first, so it needs neither root nor host file access while the daemon answers — it works from a cell that has the daemon socket mounted. The kuke serve web UI uses the same method on its Daemon → Logs page. When the daemon cannot be reached (socket missing, connection refused, permission denied, or a kukeond too old to serve the method), it falls back to reading the log file in-process, which needs root — the same read as before, so a crashed or wedged kukeond whose cell still reads as running keeps its log readable. KUKEON_NO_DAEMON=true, an explicit --run-path, or an explicit --server-configuration skips the socket and reads in-process directly.

Flag Default Description --follow, -f false Tail until SIGINT instead of printing current contents and exiting

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Bring the daemon back after a host reboot
sudo kuke daemon start

# Graceful restart after editing /etc/kukeon/kukeond.yaml
sudo kuke daemon restart

# Force-kill an unresponsive daemon
sudo kuke daemon kill

# Dev loop: blow away the daemon cell and re-init
sudo kuke daemon reset
sudo kuke init --kukeond-image docker.io/library/kukeon-local:dev

# Pick up a new kukeond image without a full kuke init
sudo kuke daemon recreate --kukeond-image docker.io/library/kukeon-local:dev

# Wipe /opt/kukeon/kuke-system too (user-realm data stays)
sudo kuke daemon reset --purge-system

# Tail the daemon log live
sudo kuke daemon logs -f

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• kuke init — provisions the daemon cell that kuke daemon … manages
  • kuke uninstall — full-host teardown; the next step up from daemon reset --purge-system
  • kukeond — the daemon binary itself

docs.title: kuke delete
docs.text:
Delete a resource. Can be called per-resource (kuke delete realm foo) or against a manifest (kuke delete -f file.yaml).

kuke delete <resource> <name> [--cascade] [--force] [scope flags]
kuke delete -f <file>
kuke d      <resource> <name> ...                                # alias

docs.title: Persistent flags (inherited by every subcommand)
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --cascade false Recursively delete child resources (realm → spaces → stacks → cells) --force false Skip validation; attempt deletion anyway --file, -f (empty) Delete the resources listed in a YAML file --output, -o (empty) Output format: json, yaml

Plus all global flags.

docs.title: kuke delete realm
docs.text: kuke delete realm <name> [--cascade] [--force]

docs.title: kuke delete space
docs.text: kuke delete space <name> --realm <realm> [--cascade] [--force]

docs.title: kuke delete stack
docs.text: kuke delete stack <name> --realm <r> --space <s> [--cascade] [--force]

docs.title: kuke delete cell
docs.text: kuke delete cell <name> --realm <r> --space <s> --stack <t> [--cascade] [--force]

docs.title: kuke delete blueprint
docs.text:
kuke delete blueprint <name> --realm <r> [--space <s>] [--stack <t>] [--force]

Removes the daemon-stored CellBlueprint document bound to the named scope. Cells previously materialised from this blueprint are independent copies and are not affected. --cascade does not apply — a Blueprint has no children in the resource hierarchy.

docs.title: kuke delete config
docs.text:
kuke delete config <name> --realm <r> [--space <s>] [--stack <t>] [--force]

Removes the daemon-stored CellConfig document bound to the named scope. The cells the Config stamped are not torn down — a Config is a 1:N binding, so it may have many live cells, each its own identity; delete them separately with kuke delete cell <name>. For every live cell still carrying this Config's kukeon.io/config lineage label, kuke delete config emits a one-line notice pointing at that cell to delete (never a refusal). --cascade does not apply — a Config has no children in the resource hierarchy.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Without --cascade, delete fails if the resource has children. It refuses to leave orphaned subtrees behind.
  2. With --cascade, children are deleted first (depth-first), then the parent. A realm cascade walks every space, stack, cell, and containerd container in it.
  3. With --force, validation is skipped — Kukeon will attempt to delete the metadata and tear down runtime state even when the host is in an unexpected state. Use it to recover from half-deleted resources.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Delete an empty cell
sudo kuke delete cell web --realm default --space blog --stack wordpress

# Cascade-delete an entire user realm (all spaces, stacks, cells)
sudo kuke delete realm mytenant --cascade

# Delete every resource listed in a manifest
sudo kuke delete -f site.yaml

# Remove a daemon-stored CellBlueprint (materialised cells are untouched)
sudo kuke delete blueprint dev --realm kuke-system

# Remove a daemon-stored CellConfig (the live cell it owns is not torn down)
sudo kuke delete config kukeon-dev --realm kuke-system

docs.title: delete vs. purge
docs.text:
• delete removes metadata and releases runtime state. If a detail fails (a cgroup that won't rmdir, a bridge that's in use), the command errors out.
  • purge does everything delete does and then aggressively cleans up residual state. Use it when delete --force isn't enough.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• kuke purge — more aggressive variant
  • kuke uninstall — full-host teardown (every realm, system user/group, run path)
  • Init and reset — full-host reset workflows

docs.title: kuke doctor
docs.text:
Host pre-flight checks before kuke init. These checks read the host environment (cgroup hierarchy, controller delegation, …) and fail fast with an actionable remediation when the host would otherwise produce a cryptic mid-bootstrap error.

kuke doctor [command]

docs.title: Subcommands
docs.text: Command What it checks kuke doctor cgroups cgroup-v2 controller delegation, on the host root or any sub-tree

docs.title: kuke doctor cgroups
docs.text:
kuke doctor cgroups [name] [flags]

Compares the cgroup's available + delegated controllers against the set kukeon will enable on the kukeond bootstrap cell. Distinguishes "kernel does not support" from "parent did not delegate" so the remediation suggestion is always correct.

By default it probes any controller missing from cgroup.subtree_control with a +<ctrl> write so the cgroup-namespace trap (advertised but not delegated, write returns EOPNOTSUPP) is distinguished from "merely needs the operator to enable it". The probe is idempotent on healthy hosts and harmless on trapped ones; pass --no-probe to keep the pre-flight strictly read-only.

The --probe write requires root; kuke doctor cgroups --probe fails fast with a clear message if you forget sudo.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --scope (empty) Verify a sub-tree instead of the host root: realm, space, stack, or cell. Resolves the named object's Status.CgroupPath via the daemon and runs the controller-set check on that path. --realm (empty) Realm name (required for --scope space/stack/cell) --space (empty) Space name (required for --scope stack/cell) --stack (empty) Stack name (required for --scope cell) --root /sys/fs/cgroup Path to the cgroup-v2 root --probe true Attempt a +<ctrl> write to cgroup.subtree_control for missing controllers; disambiguates the cgroup-namespace trap --no-probe false Keep the pre-flight strictly read-only. Wins over --probe when both are set. --nested-cgroup-runtime false Check the controller set required when the kukeond cell opts into NestedCgroupRuntime --verbose-status false Print per-controller status even when the pre-flight passes

Plus all global flags.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0 — every required controller is enabled (or was enabled by the probe write).
  • non-zero — at least one controller is missing, the cgroup directory could not be read, or --probe was used without root.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Host-root pre-flight, with the default +ctrl probe write
sudo kuke doctor cgroups

# Read-only check; useful in CI before you have root
kuke doctor cgroups --no-probe

# Diagnose a mid-tree delegation gap inside a specific realm
sudo kuke doctor cgroups --scope realm --realm default

# Drill all the way down to a single cell's subtree
sudo kuke doctor cgroups --scope cell --realm default --space default --stack default web

# Print per-controller status even when the check passes
sudo kuke doctor cgroups --verbose-status

# Check the alternate controller set used by NestedCgroupRuntime cells
sudo kuke doctor cgroups --nested-cgroup-runtime

docs.title: When to run
docs.text: Run kuke doctor cgroups once before the first kuke init on a new host. If the daemon later fails to start a cell with a "controller not available" error, run --scope against the parent realm/space/stack to find the level where delegation breaks.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• kuke init — what doctor pre-flights for
  • Concepts → Cgroups — the controller model

docs.title: kuke get
docs.text:
List or describe resources.

kuke get <resource> [NAME] [flags]
kuke g   <resource> [NAME] [flags]      # alias

Resources: realm, space, stack, cell, container, image, blueprint, config. Each subcommand also accepts its plural (realms, spaces, …, images, blueprints, configs) and a short alias (r, sp, st, ce, co, img, bp, cfg).

docs.title: Common flags
docs.text:
Flag Description --output, -o Output format: yaml, json, table, wide. Default: table for both a list and a single named resource (#1323). wide accepted by every kuke get <kind> for symmetry; per-kind wide columns vary (see each kind). --selector, -l Label selector (kubectl-style) to filter list results. Supports =, ==, !=, existence (key), absence (!key), and comma-separated AND (e.g. env=prod,tier!=db or env,!debug). Rejected with a positional NAME.

Plus all global flags. Every kuke get <kind> accepts the explicit --no-daemon flag to bypass the daemon (inherited as a persistent flag from the parent get command); KUKEON_NO_DAEMON=true and --run-path /opt/kukeon (which auto-promotes the command into in-process mode) work as well.

docs.title: Hierarchy flags
docs.text:
Each subcommand takes the flags that scope the query:

Subcommand Scope flags get realm [name] none (realms are top-level) get space [name] --realm (default default) get stack [name] --realm, --space get cell [name] --realm, --space, --stack get container [name] --realm, --space, --stack, --cell get image [ref] --realm (omit for cross-realm listing; defaults to default on the describe path) get blueprint [name] --realm, --space, --stack (no --cell — Blueprints are never cell-scoped) get config [name] --realm, --space, --stack (no --cell — Configs are never cell-scoped)

All scope flags default to default. See the realm default note.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• List (no positional arg): returns every resource matching the scope flags. Default output is a table.
  • Single (positional arg): returns the one matching resource. Default output is a single table row with the same columns as the list view (#1323, kubectl parity); -o wide renders the single wide row. The full document is reached via -o yaml / -o json. (Breaking change: scripts that relied on a bare named get emitting YAML must switch to -o yaml.)

docs.title: Default tables and -o wide columns
docs.text:
Per-kind column contracts. The default table is what kuke get <kind> (no -o wide) emits; -o wide appends the listed extras.

Kind Default columns -o wide appends realm NAME STATE AGE NAMESPACE space NAME REALM STATE AGE EGRESS NET-DEFAULTS stack NAME REALM SPACE STATE AGE (none — stack carries no wide-only signals) cell NAME REALM SPACE STACK STATE SYNC AGE CONTAINERS BRIDGE DIVERGENCE container NAME REALM SPACE STACK CELL STATE RESTARTS AGE IMAGE EXIT image NAME REALM CREATED (cross-realm default) DIGEST blueprint NAME REALM SPACE STACK AGE (none) config NAME REALM SPACE STACK SCHEDULE NEXT CONNECTORS secret NAME TYPE CONNECTOR REALM SPACE STACK CELL IDENTITY

SYNC (InSync/OutOfSync/-) is computed for cells that carry a kukeon.io/config=<name> lineage label; non-lineage cells render -. The -o wide DIVERGENCE column expands an OutOfSync cell with a one-line summary of what diverged (image, env, mounts, …). See kuke restart for the reconcile verb.

SCHEDULE and NEXT are filled for a CellConfig with a spec.schedule and empty otherwise. SCHEDULE is the cron expression, followed by the time zone in parentheses when one is set. NEXT is the next fire time in UTC, or suspended; it stays empty until kukeond's first scheduler pass after the schedule was applied, at most a minute. kuke get config <name> -o yaml shows the full status.schedule.

-o wide on config adds CONNECTORS: one <connector>=<what fills it> entry per connector the Config requires — the identity and the level it comes from (github=work-github (realm)), the method of a connector that keeps a login in the state volume (claude=login), MISSING for a required connector nothing resolves (a cell cannot be created from the Config until one does), and none for a connector the cell starts without. The same resolution is in status.connectors of -o yaml / -o json.

secret lists each secret's TYPE and the CONNECTOR it is an identity of; -o wide adds its readable IDENTITY fields. No output format carries secret material.

kuke get realm -o yaml and -o json never print a registry password: an inline spec.registryCredentials[].password is omitted from every output, and a Secret-backed entry shows only its secretRef.

-o wide on space surfaces the egress allowlist (EGRESS) and the cell-default-deny posture (NET-DEFAULTS yes/no).

-o wide on container surfaces the resolved container image reference (IMAGE) and the <exitCode>/<exitSignal> pair (EXIT) when either field is non-zero. The RESTARTS column lives in the default table; CGROUP, ROOT, and IMAGE (as defaults) were retired in v0.6.0 — see "Retired in v0.6.0" below.

# Table of realms — the dev-init parity check expects this column shape
sudo kuke get realms
NAME         STATE  AGE
-----------  -----  ---
default      Ready  <age>
kuke-system  Ready  <age>

# Same data with the namespace surfaced
sudo kuke get realms -o wide
NAME         STATE  AGE  NAMESPACE
-----------  -----  ---  ---------------------
default      Ready  <a>  default.kukeon.io
kuke-system  Ready  <a>  kuke-system.kukeon.io

# Single realm as YAML
sudo kuke get realm default -o yaml

# Single realm as JSON
sudo kuke get realm default -o json

# Spaces in the default realm
sudo kuke get spaces --realm default

# Cells in a stack — SYNC column flags Config-lineage drift; OutOfSync points at `kuke restart`
sudo kuke get cells --realm default --space default --stack default
NAME           REALM    SPACE    STACK    STATE  SYNC       AGE
-------------  -------  -------  -------  -----  ---------  ---
work-001       default  default  default  Ready  InSync     12m
work-002       default  default  default  Ready  OutOfSync  3m
shell          default  default  default  Ready  -          1h

# Containers — RESTARTS column (process bounces since cell start); -o wide adds IMAGE EXIT
sudo kuke get containers --realm default --space default --stack default --cell work-001 -o wide

# All containers in a cell
sudo kuke get containers --realm default --space default --stack default --cell hello-world

# Images across every realm (cross-realm by default)
sudo kuke get images

# Narrow to one realm; -o wide adds CREATED and DIGEST columns
sudo kuke get image --realm kuke-system -o wide

# Describe a single image as YAML (defaults --realm to `default` on this path)
sudo kuke get image docker.io/library/nginx:alpine -o yaml

# List every daemon-stored CellBlueprint bound to the kuke-system realm
sudo kuke get blueprints --realm kuke-system

# Show one CellConfig as YAML
sudo kuke get config kukeon-dev --realm kuke-system -o yaml

docs.title: Label selector (-l/--selector)
docs.text:
Filter list results by label query. The flag is wired on every kuke get <kind> verb (realm, space, stack, cell, container).

# Cells labeled env=prod
sudo kuke get cell -l env=prod

# Cells with the `debug` label absent
sudo kuke get cell -l '!debug'

# Comma-separated AND
sudo kuke get cell -l 'env=prod,tier!=db'

A positional NAME plus -l is rejected — a selector queries the list path, a name queries the single-resource path; mixing them is ambiguous. Malformed selectors fail before any controller call.

docs.title: get vs refresh
docs.text: get reads metadata. It does not reconcile or update .status. If you want the status to reflect the live runtime state (after a crash, or after containerd reported a change), run kuke refresh first.

docs.title: Retired in v0.6.0
docs.text:
• --show-controllers / CGROUP column — the cgroup-controllers signal on -o wide cell/container tables is gone. The state-of-cgroup-controllers check moved into kuke status's host section and kuke doctor cgroups.
  • IMAGE as a default container column — IMAGE is now an -o wide extension only. Use kuke get container -o wide or -o yaml to surface it.
  • ROOT column — retired entirely.
  • kuke image get / kuke image ls / kuke image list — folded into kuke get image[s] with no alias window. See the kuke get image examples below.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• kuke refresh — rehydrate .status from containerd/CNI
  • Manifest Reference — the full shape of what -o yaml returns

docs.title: kuke health
docs.text:
kuke health [--since <duration|RFC3339|last-report>] [-o text|json|yaml] [--exit-code]
kuke health reports [-o text|json|yaml]
kuke health report <id|latest> [-o markdown|json|yaml]
kuke health report submit -f <file> [--file-issues <owner>/<repo>]
kuke health issue -f <file>

kuke health shows kukeond's health digest: host and state checks, the error-level entries of kukeond's own log, and the cells in a failed state. The subcommands read and write health reports, the triaged result of a majordomo health sweep.

The digest is computed inside kukeond, by plain code with no model involved. kuke only asks for it over the daemon socket, so the answer describes the host whether you run kuke health on the host or in a cell that mounts the kukeond socket.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --since 1h Start of the log window: a duration (90m), an RFC3339 time, or last-report. -o text Output format: text, json or yaml. --exit-code false Exit 2 when the digest has findings. Without it, a digest with findings exits 0.

Plus all global flags. kuke health always talks to kukeond; it has no --no-daemon mode.

--since last-report starts the window at the end (until) of the newest stored report, so consecutive sweeps neither overlap nor leave a gap. With no report stored it falls back to one hour.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 The digest is clean, or --exit-code was not given. 2 --exit-code was given and the digest has findings. Nothing is printed to stderr. 1 The command failed: kukeond unreachable, an invalid flag, a rejected report.

docs.title: What the digest contains
docs.text:
Checks. The host and state set that kuke status reports, evaluated in kukeond instead of in the client:

Check Fails or warns when host/containerd kukeond cannot reach the containerd socket (fail). host/cgroup-v2 cgroup-v2 is not mounted (fail) or advertises no controllers (warn). host/cni-plugins bridge or loopback is missing where kukeond executes CNI plugins (fail). state/run-dir The kukeond socket directory holds entries kukeon does not own (warn). state/containerd-ns A kukeon containerd namespace is claimed by no realm (warn).

host/cni-plugins differs from the kuke status row on purpose. kuke status looks at the host's /opt/cni/bin, which kukeon does not use; the digest looks at the plugins bundled in kukeond's image, which is where cell networking runs them. A missing plugin there is a failure.

Log errors. Error-level entries of kukeond's log inside the window, grouped by signature. The signature is the entry's message and error text with timestamps, identifiers and numbers masked, so start cell failed: task 4f1b2b0b822c: exit status 1 and the same failure for another task are one group. Each group has a count, first and last seen time, and its newest entry as a sample. When kukeond has no log file (it runs outside its cell), the digest says so in logNote and the other sections still apply.

Cells. Every cell currently in Failed or Error, whatever the window, with its full scope and the time it entered the state. Failed is kukeon's own bring-up failure and is tagged kukeon; Error is a workload that exited non-zero and is tagged workload. kukeon records no state transition time, so the time is the newest container finish time for an Error cell and the cell's last status write otherwise.

A digest is clean when every check is ok, no log group fell in the window and no cell is listed.

docs.title: Digest schema
docs.text:
-o json and -o yaml print this shape. schemaVersion is kukeon.io/health/v1; it changes only if a field is removed or changes meaning. New fields may be added without a version change.

{
  "schemaVersion": "kukeon.io/health/v1",
  "since": "2026-11-17T09:00:00Z",
  "until": "2026-11-17T10:00:00Z",
  "clean": false,
  "checks": [
    {
      "section": "host",
      "name": "cni-plugins",
      "status": "fail",
      "detail": "/opt/cni/bin (missing: bridge)",
      "remediation": "redeploy kukeond from an image that bundles the CNI plugins: `kuke init --kukeond-image <image>`"
    }
  ],
  "logErrors": [
    {
      "signature": "start cell failed: task <id>: exit status <n>",
      "count": 3,
      "firstSeen": "2026-11-17T09:12:04Z",
      "lastSeen": "2026-11-17T09:48:51Z",
      "sample": "time=2026-11-17T09:48:51.120Z level=ERROR msg=\"start cell failed\" error=\"task 4f1b2b0b822c: exit status 1\""
    }
  ],
  "logSource": "/opt/kukeon/data/kuke-system/kukeon/kukeon/kukeond/kukeond/log",
  "cells": [
    {
      "realm": "default",
      "space": "default",
      "stack": "default",
      "name": "api",
      "state": "Failed",
      "classification": "kukeon",
      "since": "2026-11-17T09:48:51Z",
      "reason": "CreateFailed",
      "message": "cni attach failed"
    }
  ]
}
Field Values checks[].status ok, warn, fail checks[].remediation Present only when the check is not ok and a fix is known. logSource The log file read. Absent, with logNote set, when it could not be read. cells[].classification kukeon or workload cells[].reason/message kukeond's own description of the state; absent when it recorded none.

docs.title: kuke health reports
docs.text: Lists the reports kukeond stores, newest first: id, creation time, and how many findings each has, how many were recurring and how many were filed. -o json prints an array ([] when there are none).

docs.title: kuke health report
docs.text:
kuke health report <id> prints one report; latest selects the newest. The default output is markdown for reading. -o json and -o yaml print the stored document.

kukeond keeps the newest 50 reports and drops older ones on each submission. Reports are files under kukeond's run path, so they survive a kukeond restart. They are operational state, not a system of record: storing a report files nothing anywhere.

docs.title: kuke health report submit
docs.text:
kuke health report submit -f <file> validates a report document and stores it. -f - reads stdin. The document is JSON or YAML, and unknown fields are rejected.

since: 2026-11-17T09:00:00Z
until: 2026-11-17T10:00:00Z
cell: { realm: default, space: default, stack: default, name: sweep-1a2b3c }
summary: One kukeon defect, one workload failure.
findings:
  - signature: "cell default/default/default/api Failed"
    classification: kukeon
    severity: error
    title: "api fails to start: CNI attach error"
    evidence:
      - "status.reason: CreateFailed"
    suggestedCommands:
      - "kuke restart api --realm default --space default --stack default"
body: |
  # Health sweep
  ...
Field Required Notes id no kukeond assigns one when omitted. A duplicate id, or latest, is rejected. createdAt no kukeond sets it when omitted. since, until yes The digest window the report covers; until must not precede since. cell yes realm, space, stack and name of the submitting cell. summary yes findings yes A list; [] is valid. body no Markdown. findings[].signature yes Unique within the report. Identifies the finding across reports. findings[].classification yes kukeon, workload or unclear. findings[].severity yes info, warning, error or critical. findings[].evidence yes At least one entry. findings[].title no findings[].count no Occurrences in the window. findings[].suggestedCommands no Commands for the reader. Nothing runs them. findings[].issueUrl no An https URL, allowed only on a kukeon finding. findings[].recurring — Computed by kukeond; a submitted value is ignored.

On submission kukeond marks a finding recurring when the previous stored report already carried the same signature. A hand-started sweep that overlaps a scheduled one therefore reports the same finding as recurring, not as new.

docs.title: Filing issues (opt-in)
docs.text:
By default nothing is filed. --file-issues <owner>/<repo> makes kuke first validate the report the way kukeond will (a report kukeond would reject files nothing), then, before it stores the report:

  • open one GitHub issue for each kukeon finding, titled health: <area>: <symptom>, whose body has the symptom, the evidence, the frequency and the kukeon version;
  • add a comment instead when an open issue already carries the finding's signature;
  • record the issue URL in the report.

workload and unclear findings are never filed. Before anything is sent, evidence is stripped of secret values and credential-bearing URLs: known token formats, key=value pairs whose key names a credential, private key blocks and URL userinfo.

Filing needs a GitHub token in the GH_TOKEN environment variable, which the github connector sets once the install binds the gh-token secret to the majordomo role. Without it, --file-issues fails naming GH_TOKEN and the opt-in, and the report is still stored. If filing fails, the report is still stored and the command exits 1. If the report cannot be stored after filing ran, the command prints the issues it opened or commented on to stderr and exits 1. See opting in to filing for how an install turns it on. KUKE_HEALTH_GITHUB_API overrides the API base URL for GitHub Enterprise.

docs.title: Rendering an issue for a diagnosed defect
docs.text:
kuke health issue -f draft.yaml

kuke health issue renders a kukeon defect found outside a sweep, by an interactive majordomo investigation, as the title, body, comment and signature marker a GitHub issue for it carries. It prints JSON and files nothing: the majordomo file-kukeon-bug skill files the result with gh. It uses the same title format, sanitizer and kukeon-health-signature marker as --file-issues, so an issue filed from it and a sweep-filed issue for the same signature dedupe against each other. The value of GH_TOKEN, when set, is redacted as well.

The draft (JSON or YAML; - reads stdin) has the fields below. Unknown fields are rejected, and a draft not classified kukeon is refused.

Field Required Notes signature yes The sweep's signature when one applies, so the markers match. classification yes Must be kukeon. severity yes info, warning, error or critical. evidence yes At least one entry. title no The symptom; the signature stands in when empty. reproduction no Steps or commands that reproduce the defect, rendered in their own section.

The output has title, body (a new issue's body, ending with the marker), comment (the note for an open issue that already carries the marker) and marker. The kukeon version comes from kukeond, or reads unknown when it is unreachable.

docs.title: When to use kuke health vs kuke status
docs.text:
kuke status kuke health Evaluated by the kuke client kukeond Run inside a cell host and state rows describe the cell's container describes the host Covers daemon liveness, host, state, storage, daemon parity host, state, kukeond log errors, failed cells Needs kukeond no yes

Use kuke status on the host after kuke init, including when kukeond is down. Use kuke health for a running install, and always from inside a cell.

docs.text:

  • Teams → The majordomo health sweep

docs.title: kuke image
docs.text:
Manage container images in a realm's containerd namespace.

kuke image [command]

Every realm maps to its own containerd namespace (<realm>.kukeon.io). kuke image loads and deletes images inside that namespace. The default realm is default (containerd namespace default.kukeon.io); pass --realm kuke-system to operate on the system realm where the kukeond image lives.

Images land in a realm via one of two producers: kuke build builds an OCI image from a Dockerfile straight into the realm's containerd namespace, and kuke image load imports a pre-built OCI/docker tarball into the same namespace.

Listing and describing images moved to the kuke get family in #824 — use kuke get image[s] for both the cross-realm default and the single-image describe form. The old kuke image get / kuke image ls / kuke image list aliases are gone (no deprecation window).

docs.title: Subcommands
docs.text: Command What it does kuke image load Import an OCI/docker image tarball into a realm's containerd namespace kuke image delete Remove an image from a realm's containerd namespace kuke image prune Reclaim dangling image layers and orphaned leases in a realm

docs.title: kuke image load
docs.text:
kuke image load [tarball | -] [flags]

Import an OCI/docker image tarball into the containerd namespace mapped to --realm. Pass a tarball path, - for stdin, or --from-docker <ref> to shell out to docker save.

kuke image * is daemon-independent by design: every subcommand wraps containerd's image API directly in-process — there is no "with daemon" mode for images, and the --no-daemon flag is intentionally absent on these commands. kuke image load always requires root because it writes to containerd's content store; it fails fast with a clear remediation if you forget sudo.

Flag Default Description --from-docker (empty) Image reference to pipe in via docker save <ref> (mutually exclusive with the positional tarball) --realm default Target realm; the image lands in <realm>.kukeon.io

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Load a saved tarball into the default realm
sudo kuke image load my-image.tar

# Pipe a docker-build into kuke-system for a local kukeond image
sudo kuke image load --from-docker kukeon-local:dev --realm kuke-system

# Stdin
docker save myimage:latest | sudo kuke image load -

docs.title: kuke image delete
docs.text:
kuke image delete <ref> [flags]
kuke image rm     <ref> [flags]      # alias
Flag Default Description --realm default Target realm; the lookup runs in <realm>.kukeon.io

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Remove an image from the default realm
sudo kuke image delete docker.io/library/nginx:alpine

# Remove an image from kuke-system
sudo kuke image delete docker.io/library/kukeon-local:dev --realm kuke-system

docs.title: kuke image prune
docs.text:
kuke image prune [flags]

Reclaim dangling image layers and orphaned leases in a realm.

kuke image prune reclaims dangling image layers and orphaned content leases in the target realm's containerd namespace, then reports how many leases were released versus retained. It takes no positional arguments.

Flag Default Description --realm default Target realm; the prune runs in <realm>.kukeon.io

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Prune the default realm
sudo kuke image prune

# Prune kuke-system
sudo kuke image prune --realm kuke-system

Sample output:

pruned realm "default" (namespace "default.kukeon.io"): released 3 lease(s), retained 12

docs.text:

docs.title: kuke init
docs.text:
Bootstrap or reconcile a host. Creates the kukeon cgroup root, the CNI config directory, both default realms (default and kuke-system) and their default space/stack, and the kukeond cell. Starts the daemon and waits for it to respond.

kuke init [flags]

Always runs as root: it touches /sys/fs/cgroup, containerd namespaces, /opt/kukeon, and CNI dirs. kuke init fails fast with a clear remediation if you forget sudo.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --realm default Name of the default user realm --space default Name of the default space inside the user realm --kukeond-image ghcr.io/eminwux/kukeon:<version> Image to run the daemon cell. See image resolution. --server-configuration /etc/kukeon/kukeond.yaml ServerConfiguration YAML to seed the daemon with; absent file uses hardcoded defaults --cgroup-root /kukeon Cgroup root under which all realms / spaces / stacks / cells live --containerd-namespace-suffix kukeon.io Suffix appended to every realm name to form its containerd namespace (default → default.kukeon.io) --no-wait false Don't wait for the daemon socket after bootstrap --force-regenerate-cni false Rewrite every space's CNI conflist even if it exists. See Troubleshooting.

Plus all global flags.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Creates /sys/fs/cgroup/kukeon if missing (or the directory matching --cgroup-root).
  2. Creates /etc/cni/net.d and /opt/cni/bin if missing.
  3. Creates the user realm (--realm, default default): containerd namespace <realm>.kukeon.io, cgroup, metadata. The realm is left empty so kuke purge --cascade on it can never take down the daemon.
  4. Creates the default space (--space, default default) inside the user realm: CNI conflist, bridge, cgroup, metadata.
  5. Creates the default stack (default) inside the default space: cgroup, metadata.
  6. Creates the system realm kuke-system (containerd namespace kuke-system.kukeon.io), plus its kukeon space and kukeon stack.
  7. Creates the kukeond cell inside kuke-system / kukeon / kukeon and its root container using --kukeond-image.
  8. Starts the daemon's root container; waits up to 30s for the socket to accept a Ping RPC (skipped when --no-wait is set). The socket is chowned to the kukeon system group with mode 0660 so members of that group can dial it.

Everything is idempotent. Re-running init on a bootstrapped host reports already existed for the parts it finds on disk. Use --force-regenerate-cni to explicitly rewrite the CNI conflist.

docs.title: The two default realms
docs.text:
kuke init provisions two realms, each mapped to its own containerd namespace:

Realm Containerd namespace Purpose default default.kukeon.io User workloads. Created empty so kuke create … has a home. kuke-system kuke-system.kukeon.io System workloads owned by kukeon itself.

The kukeond daemon runs as a container inside the cell kuke-system / kukeon / kukeon / kukeond. The default realm is deliberately left user-owned so kuke purge --cascade on it can never take down the daemon.

docs.title: Image resolution
docs.text:
--kukeond-image takes precedence. When not set, Kukeon composes the image reference from build-time constants:

  • Release builds: ghcr.io/eminwux/kukeon:<version> where <version> is the semver tag.
  • Dev builds (no tag or non-v-prefixed version): ghcr.io/eminwux/kukeon:latest.

For local iteration, pre-load a local image with kuke image load --from-docker and pass --kukeond-image docker.io/library/kukeon-local:dev or whatever tag you built.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Fresh bootstrap with defaults
sudo kuke init

# Bootstrap with a different user-realm name
sudo kuke init --realm myenv --space default

# Local dev: point at a hand-loaded image
sudo kuke init --kukeond-image docker.io/library/kukeon-local:dev

# Re-init with CNI regeneration (recovers from stale conflist)
sudo kuke init --force-regenerate-cni

# Bootstrap without waiting for the daemon to come up
sudo kuke init --no-wait

# Run host pre-flight before initializing
sudo kuke doctor cgroups
sudo kuke init

docs.title: Output
docs.text: init prints a structured bootstrap report: what was created, what already existed, and the resulting runtime path. A fresh bootstrap example is in Getting Started.
