  • kuke daemon — lifecycle verbs for the kukeond cell after bootstrap
  • Init and reset — teardown, re-init, and reset workflows
  • Local development — first-time bootstrap with a local image

docs.title: kuke start / stop / kill
docs.text:
Runtime lifecycle for cells. These commands don't touch metadata — they operate on the containerd task under the resource.

Command Signal What it does kuke start (create/start task) Launch the container(s); no-op if already running kuke stop SIGTERM Graceful shutdown; SIGKILL after a short grace period kuke kill SIGKILL Immediate termination; no graceful shutdown window

All three take the same shape: <verb> <name> <scope flags>. The <name> positional resolves to a cell within the named realm/space/stack — cells are the only lifecycle subject.

docs.title: kuke start
docs.text:
kuke start (<name> | -l <selector>) --realm <r> --space <s> --stack <t>

Aliases: kuke start → kuke sta.

start starts the cell's root container first, then every non-root container in the cell.

With -l <selector> (mutually exclusive with the positional <name>) the start fans out across every cell in scope whose labels match, reconciling each matched cell individually. Unmatched cells are untouched.

docs.title: kuke stop
docs.text:
kuke stop <name> --realm <r> --space <s> --stack <t>

Aliases: kuke stop → kuke sto.

Sends SIGTERM to every task in the cell: the workload containers first, then the root container. If a container has a shutdown handler, it gets a chance to run. A task still running after a short grace period (5s; there is no flag to change it today) is sent SIGKILL. stop waits for each task to exit and deletes it, including tasks that had already exited, then releases the cell's network.

docs.title: kuke kill
docs.text:
kuke kill <name> --realm <r> --space <s> --stack <t>

Aliases: kuke kill → kuke k.

Sends SIGKILL to every task in the cell, workloads first, then the root. Like stop, it waits for each task to exit and deletes it, so the two verbs leave the same end state; they differ only in the first signal. Useful when a cell is unresponsive. For the daemon itself, prefer the dedicated kuke daemon kill shortcut — it knows the daemon's static coordinates.

docs.title: Common flags
docs.text:
All three verbs share the same scope flags:

Flag Default Scope --realm default Required for cell --space default Required for cell --stack default Required for cell

kuke start additionally accepts -l, --selector (start-only among the three verbs): Label selector (e.g. kukeon.io/config=<name>); starts every matched cell in scope. Mutually exclusive with <name>.

Plus all global flags.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Start a cell
sudo kuke start web --realm default --space blog --stack wordpress

# Graceful stop
sudo kuke stop web --realm default --space blog --stack wordpress

# Force-kill an unresponsive cell
sudo kuke kill web --realm default --space blog --stack wordpress

docs.title: Exit semantics
docs.text:
• Exit 0: signal delivered (or cell already in desired state for start).
  • Exit non-zero: the daemon couldn't find the resource, the resource is in a state that doesn't allow the transition, or the underlying containerd/runtime call failed.

After stop/kill, no task of the cell is left behind. The state the cell is left in depends on what the verb interrupted:

  • The cell had already settled in Exited or Error and no workload was running: the state, REASON and MESSAGE are kept.
  • A workload was still running, the cell was Degraded, or a restart was owed: Stopped with reason OperatorStopped. This suppresses --rm auto-delete until the cell is restarted or deleted.
  • Otherwise: Stopped.

Stopping or killing an already torn-down cell is a no-op that exits 0. start moves the cell to Ready. See Cell and Container for the full state tables.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• kuke run — create + start a cell from a file or profile
  • kuke daemon — start/stop/restart/kill the kukeond daemon cell

docs.title: kuke log
docs.text:
Print a container's stdout/stderr stream.

kuke log  <cell> [flags]
kuke logs <cell> [flags]      # alias

<cell> is a positional argument. --realm, --space, and --stack all default to default, so for a cell in the default location you only need the cell name.

By default, kuke log prints the current contents of the capture file and exits. Pass -f/--follow to tail until SIGINT.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --container (auto-pick) Container within the cell to read (omit to auto-pick the only non-root container) --realm default Realm that owns the cell --space default Space that owns the cell --stack default Stack that owns the cell --follow, -f false Tail the file until SIGINT instead of printing current contents and exiting

Plus all global flags.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
kuke log asks the daemon for the container's output stream — the sbsh capture of an attachable container, or the runtime log of any other — and prints the bytes exactly as stored, including terminal escape sequences and a trailing prompt with no newline. The bytes travel over the kukeond socket in bounded chunks, so kuke log needs only access to the socket (KUKEON_HOST), not to the host's /opt/kukeon: it works the same from a cell that mounts just the kukeond socket and the kuke binary. Without -f, it prints what's there and exits — useful for scripting and for checking on a container that has already terminated. With -f, it keeps polling for new bytes until you SIGINT (Ctrl-C) the command; if the stream is truncated or replaced, it starts again from the beginning of the new stream.

kuke log shows the live capture only: when sbsh has rotated older output into closed segments, those are not reassembled.

With KUKEON_NO_DAEMON=true (or an explicit --run-path), kuke log reads the same stream in-process from the host's /opt/kukeon. Against a kukeond too old to serve the chunked read, kuke log falls back to resolving the file's host path through the daemon and opening it directly, which again requires the host's /opt/kukeon.

Container selection: if the cell has exactly one non-root container, --container can be omitted. Otherwise, pass --container explicitly.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Print and exit (cell in default/default/default)
sudo kuke log web

# Follow until Ctrl-C
sudo kuke log web -f

# Explicit container in a multi-container cell
sudo kuke log web --container nginx -f

# Non-default realm/space/stack
sudo kuke log wp --realm default --space blog --stack wordpress

docs.title: kuke log vs. kuke daemon logs
docs.text: kuke log is for any user-workload container. To read the kukeond daemon's own logs without typing out the static kuke-system / kukeon / kukeon / kukeond coordinates, use kuke daemon logs — the same stream for the kukeond container, with the realm/space/stack/cell pre-filled.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• kuke daemon logs — shortcut for the daemon's own log stream
  • kuke attach — interactive sbsh terminal instead of a one-way log stream

docs.title: kuke purge
docs.text:
More aggressive variant of kuke delete. Removes metadata, releases runtime state, and cleans up residual artifacts (cgroups, CNI networks, containerd remnants) that delete would leave behind on error.

kuke purge <resource> <name> [--cascade] [--force] [scope flags]
kuke p     <resource> <name> ...                                # alias

Resources: realm, space, stack, cell.

docs.title: Persistent flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --cascade false Recursively purge children --force false Skip validation; attempt purge regardless of current state

Plus all global flags.

docs.title: Per-resource subcommands
docs.text:
Shape and flags are identical to the equivalent delete subcommands:

kuke purge realm <name>                                         [--cascade] [--force]
kuke purge space <name> --realm <r>                             [--cascade] [--force]
kuke purge stack <name> --realm <r> --space <s>                 [--cascade] [--force]
kuke purge cell  <name> --realm <r> --space <s> --stack <t>     [--cascade] [--force]

docs.title: When to use purge vs. delete
docs.text:
• Use delete when the host is in a healthy state. It's the safer option; it won't blow past a validation failure.
  • Use purge when delete --force errors out or leaves residue (a cgroup directory that won't rmdir, a bridge that wasn't torn down, a containerd container that's stuck). It's the hammer.

docs.title: What purge does that delete doesn't
docs.text:
purge still goes through the same reconciliation, but after every step it verifies the state is actually gone and tries harder if not:

  • Cgroup directories that refuse to remove are retried after freezing and killing residents.
  • Containerd containers left behind (for any reason) are force-deleted from the namespace.
  • CNI networks are torn down via the bridge plugin even when the metadata is inconsistent.
  • Conflist files are unlinked from disk.

docs.title: Safe by design: purging the user realm
docs.text:
kuke purge --cascade on the default (user) realm is safe: the daemon lives in kuke-system / kukeon / kukeon / kukeond, so the user-realm cascade can never take down the daemon. To wipe default and immediately reuse the host:

sudo kuke purge realm default --cascade --force
sudo kuke create realm default
sudo kuke create space  default --realm default
sudo kuke create stack  default --realm default --space default

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Purge a user realm that delete wouldn't tear down
sudo kuke purge realm mytenant --cascade --force

# Nuke a broken cell
sudo kuke purge cell stuck --realm default --space default --stack default --cascade --force

docs.title: Caution
docs.text:
purge is destructive and makes "best effort" its primary operating mode. It will keep going past errors that would halt delete. Use it when you're prepared to lose state that you didn't explicitly back up.

For a full-host teardown (every realm, the kukeon system user/group, and /opt/kukeon itself), use kuke uninstall.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• kuke delete — the safer variant
  • kuke uninstall — per-host teardown wrapping purge --cascade
  • Init and reset → Full host wipe — uses purge --cascade --force in the nuclear path

docs.title: kuke refresh
docs.text:
Reconcile .status from the live runtime without touching .spec.

kuke refresh

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Walks every realm / space / stack / cell / container that Kukeon has metadata for, asks containerd and CNI what the actual state is, and updates the .status field of each resource on disk. It does not modify .spec or any runtime state.

Use it when:

  • A container crashed and Kukeon's status is still Ready — refresh will update it to Error (a non-zero workload exit) or Exited (a clean exit). Failed stays reserved for Kukeon's own bring-up faults.
  • You rebooted the host (or restarted containerd) and kuke get still shows pre-reboot state.
  • You intervened outside Kukeon (ctr tasks kill, ip link delete) and want the metadata to catch up.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: None beyond the global flags.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
A summary of what was inspected and what was updated:

$ sudo kuke refresh
Inspected 2 realms, 2 spaces, 2 stacks, 1 cells, 1 containers.
Updated 0 resources.

docs.title: When it's a no-op
docs.text: If Kukeon's metadata already matches the live state — i.e., you haven't rebooted, crashed, or intervened — refresh finds nothing to update. It's safe to run at any time.

docs.title: refresh vs. get
docs.text:
• get reads metadata and prints it. It never changes anything.
  • refresh reads the live runtime and writes updated .status to disk. The next get will then reflect the new state.

So a typical "what's actually happening right now" workflow is:

sudo kuke refresh
sudo kuke get cells --realm default --space default --stack default

docs.title: kuke restart
docs.text:
kuke restart (<name> | -l <selector>) [--realm <name>] [--space <name>] [--stack <name>]

Restart a cell (cells are the only lifecycle subject). Bounces the running process. When the cell is a Config-lineage cell, the start step renders its Config at start time and, when the render differs from the cell, re-materialises the spec from it (daemon-side, in controller.StartCell — issues #983, #1569), so the restart is also a reconcile.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
kuke restart (<name> | -l <selector>) [--realm <name>] [--space <name>] [--stack <name>]

Bounces the cell's containers (stop + start). When the cell carries a kukeon.io/config=<name> lineage label, the daemon's StartCell renders the lineage Config on every start and, when the render differs from the cell, reapplies it before bringing the cell back up — equivalent to kuke stop <name> + kuke start <name>. The decision comes from that render, not from the cell's OutOfSync status, so a kuke restart straight after kuke apply of the Config runs the new spec without waiting for the reconcile tick. Severs any active attach session as a side effect of the stop step.

With -l <selector> (mutually exclusive with the positional <name>) the restart fans out across every cell in scope whose labels match, reconciling each matched cell individually — the fleet-rollout path for a Config whose stamped cells share the kukeon.io/config=<name> lineage label. Unmatched cells are untouched.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description <name> (positional) (one of) The cell to restart. Mutually exclusive with -l; exactly one of <name> / -l is required -l, --selector "" Label selector (e.g. kukeon.io/config=<name>); restarts every matched cell in scope. Mutually exclusive with <name> --realm "" Realm that owns the cell --space "" Space that owns the cell --stack "" Stack that owns the cell

Plus all global flags. Realm/space/stack are required (no default fall-through); a missing one returns the matching errdefs.ErrRealmNameRequired / ErrSpaceNameRequired / ErrStackNameRequired sentinel.

docs.title: Behavior by cell state
docs.text:
kuke restart dispatches on the cell's Status.State at the moment the command runs:

State Behavior Ready Pure bounce: StopCell then StartCell. For a Config-lineage cell the daemon's StartCell renders the lineage Config and rebuilds the cell from it when the render differs from the cell; otherwise it just starts the on-disk spec. Stopped / Exited Equivalent to kuke start <name>. Stopped is an operator stop/kill; Exited is a clean self-exit (#1267) — both restart in place. The daemon-side lineage reapply also fires here, so kuke stop + kuke start produces the same end state as kuke restart on the same cell (#983). Failed / Error / Degraded Equivalent to kuke start <name>: the daemon recovers the cell with a recreate (stop → delete → recreate containers → start, the sticky root included; #1268, #1274). For a Config-lineage cell whose Config renders to a different spec, the recreate uses that fresh spec, so a crashed cell whose Config was fixed comes back on the fix in one restart (#1569). With no lineage, a deleted Config or a render failure, it recreates from the on-disk spec. Error is the #1267 workload-crash terminal. Pending / Unknown Refused with cell "<name>" exists in <state> state; delete it with \kuke delete cell ` before restarting`. Exit code non-zero.

docs.title: OutOfSync detection
docs.text: The OutOfSync flag on a cell is set by the daemon's reconciler loop when a cell carrying a kukeon.io/config=<name> lineage label has a live spec that no longer matches the materialisation of its source Config (someone edited the Config, or the underlying Blueprint, after the cell was last materialised). Surface it ahead of kuke restart with kuke get cell <name> — the SYNC column reports InSync / OutOfSync / Unknown. The flag is informational: kuke restart does not wait for it, since the start step renders the Config itself. A successful reapply clears outOfSync, outOfSyncReason and outOfSyncError at once and records the fresh render provenance, so kuke get cell reads InSync straight after the restart. A cell without the lineage label is never marked OutOfSync, so kuke restart on such cells is always a pure bounce.

docs.title: Side effects
docs.text:
• Active attach sessions are severed by the stop step.
  • The reapply lives in the daemon's controller.StartCell (internal/controller/start_cell.go), so every code path that issues StartCell — kuke restart's start step, kuke start directly, and kuke run <cell> on an existing Stopped cell — inherits the reconcile-on-start behaviour. The CLI restart command itself no longer composes GetConfig + GetBlueprint + ApplyDocuments; those calls happen daemon-side.
  • The daemon resolves the lineage Config from the cell's render provenance (spec.provenance.bindingRef), at exactly the scope the cell was rendered from, so a same-named Config at another scope never shadows it. Only a cell without provenance falls back to probing its full scope → space-only → realm-only by the kukeon.io/config label name. It then materialises the cell from Config + Blueprint and routes the diff by change class: a Breaking change (or a realm image rebuilt under the same tag) rebuilds via RecreateCell, tearing down the stale containerd records and starting fresh containers with the new spec; a Compatible change (env, ports, volumes, spec.autoDelete, spec.tty, a workload container's image or args) is applied in place with UpdateCell, keeping the root container and its overlay; a change of render inputs that leaves the spec unchanged only records the new provenance.
  • A reapply that cannot run (lineage Config deleted, referenced Blueprint missing or any other render error, RecreateCell failure) falls back to starting the cell with the on-disk spec — the runtime still bounces as the operator asked. Diagnostics are logged daemon-side (kukeond slog stream) rather than printed to the CLI.
  • Running clones of the source Config are unaffected by a kuke restart on one cell; each clone needs its own kuke restart <clone-name> (or stop+start) to pick up the new spec.

docs.title: Example session
docs.text:
$ kuke get cell foo --realm default --space default --stack default -o wide
NAME  STATE  SYNC        AGE  ...
foo   Ready  OutOfSync   12m  ...

$ kuke restart foo --realm default --space default --stack default
Restarted cell "foo" from stack "default"

$ kuke get cell foo --realm default --space default --stack default -o wide
NAME  STATE  SYNC    AGE  ...
foo   Ready  InSync  3s   ...

The same end state is reachable via the explicit stop+start pair:

$ kuke stop foo --realm default --space default --stack default
Stopped cell "foo" from stack "default"

$ kuke start foo --realm default --space default --stack default
Started cell "foo" from stack "default"

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• kuke start / stop / kill — primitive lifecycle verbs kuke restart composes; the lineage reapply also fires from kuke start directly.
  • kuke get — read the SYNC column on kuke get cell -o wide to spot OutOfSync ahead of restart.
  • kuke run — divergent-spec warn-and-attach on the -f path (--require-synced for the opt-in refusal) cites kuke restart <name> as the reconcile pointer; kuke run <cell> on an existing Stopped cell also triggers the daemon-side reapply.
  • kind: CellConfig — the lineage source the start-time reapply re-materialises from.
  • kind: CellBlueprint — referenced by the Config, looked up via GetBlueprint on the reapply path.

docs.title: kuke run
docs.text:
kuke run is the fused docker-model verb: docker create → kuke create cell, docker start → kuke start, docker run → kuke run (create? + start + attach).

Six source paths:

  • kuke run <cell> — start + attach an existing cell (≈ kuke start <cell> + kuke attach <cell>). The cell must already exist; a missing name errors with a pointer at the create paths.
  • kuke run -f <file> — a single-cell YAML doc (or - for stdin). Create-or-attach by metadata.name.
  • kuke run --image <ref> [--command <cmd>] — synthesize a single-container cell from a bare image ref and create + start + attach it (the quick-start path). The container is attachable: true with entrypoint /bin/sh (overridable via --command); the runner synthesizes the root container at create time.
  • kuke run --from-blueprint <bp> [--param K=V]... — create + start + attach a fresh cell from a daemon-stored CellBlueprint.
  • kuke run --from-config <cfg> [--mode <m>] [--param K=V]... [--env K=V]... — create + start + attach a fresh cell from a daemon-stored CellConfig, in the picked harness mode.
  • kuke run --clone <cell> — fork an existing cell's recipe (its materialised CellDoc) into a fresh cell. Lineage and provenance binding are preserved; the source cell's runtime overlay is not copied.

The fused --from-*/--clone form delegates its create half to the same cell.Materialize function kuke create cell runs (shared FlagSet, no drift): the produced CellDoc is identical to kuke create cell --from-... followed by kuke start. The cell name is --name X when given, else a generated <prefix>-<6hex> probed free against the daemon at the cell's scope.

Drift between the live cell's spec and the materialisation of the requested source — for the -f path only — defaults to warn-and-attach (post-#986): a one-line notice: cites the diverging fields and the kuke apply -f pointer, then the operator is dropped into the live cell. Pass --require-synced for the opt-in strict mode that CI/scripted callers want — drift then refuses to attach with the same error shape the pre-#986 default emitted. The fused --from-*/--clone paths always materialise a fresh cell (refuse on --name collision rather than diverge), and the <cell> positional has no source to compare against, so --require-synced is a -f-only knob.

kuke run (<cell> | -f <file> | --image <ref> | --from-blueprint <bp> | --from-config <cfg> | --clone <cell>) [flags]

To re-attach to an already-running cell without bouncing it, use kuke attach <cell>.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description <cell> (positional) (one of <cell> / -f / --from-*/--clone) Existing cell to start + attach, resolved in the scope named by --realm/--space/--stack. A missing cell errors with a pointer at kuke create cell / kuke run --from-... --file, -f (one source) YAML to read (path or - for stdin); mutually exclusive with the <cell> positional and --image/--from-blueprint/--from-config/--clone --image (one source) Image ref to synthesize a single-container cell from (the quick-start path): create + start + attach a one-container cell running <ref> (attachable: true, entrypoint overridable via --command). Names the cell via --name, else a generated <prefix>-<6hex> derived from the image. Mutually exclusive with the <cell> positional and -f/--from-blueprint/--from-config/--clone --command (/bin/sh) With --image: override the synthesized container's entrypoint. Only valid with --image --from-blueprint (one source) Daemon-stored CellBlueprint name to materialise from, resolved from the scope named by --realm/--space/--stack. Substitutes scalar --param/--param-file values. The fused path: creates + starts + attaches a fresh cell --from-config (one source) Daemon-stored CellConfig name to materialise from, resolved from the same scope. The Config carries its own scalar values + structural slot fills, so --param-file is rejected and --param is accepted only for the parameters of the harness mode the cell is created in (--mode); persisted per-cell env overrides are supplied via --env KEY=VALUE --clone (one source) Existing cell to fork. Materialises a fresh cell from the source's CellDoc (container spec, scope, provenance binding); the runtime overlay is not copied --name (generated <prefix>-<6hex>) Name the cell created by --image/--from-blueprint/--from-config/--clone. Rejected with the <cell> positional (the positional IS the cell name) and with -f (where metadata.name is authoritative). A --name X collision against a live cell exits non-zero with a kuke run X pointer for the start+attach-existing path --mode (the Config's default) Harness mode to create the cell in (e.g. interactive, headless). Valid with --from-config and --clone of a Config-lineage cell; must be a mode the blueprint declares and the Config enables. See Modes --param (empty, repeatable) Scalar parameter override as KEY=VALUE. With --from-blueprint each KEY must be declared in spec.parameters[]; it wins over the default and over --param-file. With --from-config it is accepted only for the picked mode's parameters (e.g. --mode headless --param PROMPT=…) and is recorded on the cell. Rejected on every other source path --param-file (empty) File of KEY=VALUE lines whose values seed scalar parameters; one per line, # starts a comment. Same declaration rules as --param. CLI --param wins on dups. Rejected on every non---from-blueprint source path --env (empty, repeatable) KEY=VALUE env entry; repeatable. Dual semantics by source path: on the <cell> positional and -f paths it is transport-only runtime injection (Spec.RuntimeEnv, #834) into the attachable container's OCI process env at start time; on the --from-config/--clone paths it is the persisted per-cell override baked into the materialised CellDoc (Spec.Provenance.EnvOverrides, #1023). Rejected with --from-blueprint (use --param for render-time overrides) --connector (empty, repeatable) Per-cell identity override CONNECTOR=SECRET[@realm[/space[/stack]]]: use another stored identity for one connector of this cell. Valid with --from-config only; recorded in Spec.Provenance.connectorOverrides, so it survives kuke restart and a recreate --connector-method (empty, repeatable) Per-cell method CONNECTOR=METHOD: use another method of a connector for this cell, e.g. codex=api-key. Valid with --from-config only; recorded in Spec.Provenance.connectorMethods, so it survives kuke restart and a recreate --detach, -d false Return immediately after start without attaching --container (auto-pick) Container to attach to (attach mode only; rejected with -d). Precedence: --container > cell.tty.default > first attachable --rm false Best-effort delete the cell after it's no longer needed (any rc). See Cleanup with --rm. --require-synced false With -f: refuse to attach when the live cell's spec diverges from the on-disk manifest. Default (post-#986) is warn-and-attach: print a one-line notice: naming the diverging fields and the kuke apply -f pointer, then attach to the live state. --require-synced opt-in restores the pre-#986 refuse-on-divergence behaviour for CI/scripted callers that want a hard fail on drift --ignore-disk-pressure false Bypass kukeond's data-volume disk-pressure guard for this run. Threads transport-only onto Spec.IgnoreDiskPressure (issue #1035). Read off cmd.Flags() (the flag is registered by cell.RegisterSourceFlags, shared with kuke create cell; no viper bind on the run side) --realm (from manifest) Realm that owns the cell (overrides spec.realmId only when the doc is empty) --space (from manifest) Space that owns the cell --stack (from manifest) Stack that owns the cell --output, -o (human-readable) Output format: json, yaml

Plus all global flags.

docs.title: Attach vs. detach
docs.text:
By default, kuke run attaches to the cell's attachable container after start. Precedence for which container to attach to:

  1. --container <name> if set.
  2. The container marked tty.default: true in the cell spec.
  3. The single non-root attachable container, when there's exactly one.

Pass -d/--detach to return immediately without attaching. --container is rejected together with -d.

A clean ^]^] detach exits the CLI but leaves the cell running so you can re-attach later with kuke attach.

docs.title: Materialising from a Blueprint, Config, or sibling cell
docs.text:
The --from-blueprint/--from-config/--clone flags run daemon-stored templates (or fork an existing cell's recipe) instead of an on-disk file. They share their definitions with kuke create cell (cell.RegisterSourceFlags) so the un-fused kuke create cell --from-... + kuke start <name> and the fused kuke run --from-... produce identical CellDocs.

  • --from-blueprint <bp> — a CellBlueprint is a template with declared spec.parameters[]. Scalar --param KEY=VALUE (or --param-file) overrides the Blueprint's defaults. --env is rejected here (Blueprints take render-time --param, not runtime env overrides — cell.ValidateOverrideSymmetry enforces the rejection).
  • --from-config <cfg> — a CellConfig binds a CellBlueprint reference to concrete scalar values plus structural slot fills (repo bindings, secret references). --param-file is rejected and --param is limited to the picked mode's parameters (the Config owns its values — edit it instead); --mode picks the harness mode, and a cell that supplies a parameter only one mode declares is created in that mode. --env KEY=VALUE is the persisted per-cell override baked into the materialised CellDoc (Spec.Provenance.EnvOverrides, #1023) — symmetric with kuke create cell --from-config --env. The override survives re-resolution from provenance (P5) and kuke restart's daemon-side reconcile (P7). --connector <connector>=<secret> picks another stored identity for one connector of this cell, recorded the same way; a Config whose required connector resolves to no identity fails with an error naming the connector.
  • --clone <cell> — forks an existing cell's CellDoc into a fresh cell. The clone copies the source's container spec, scope, and provenance binding (the new cell stays tied to its original Blueprint/Config for re-resolution); it does not copy the source's runtime overlay. Use when you want a sibling of an existing dev cell that drifts independently from this point on.

The fused form is always create + start + attach: a --name X collision against a live cell exits non-zero with a kuke run X pointer for the start+attach-existing path. Without --name, the generated <prefix>-<6hex> is probed free against the daemon at the cell's scope, so the generated path can't collide.

To reconcile a live cell against its lineage Config/Blueprint after the source has changed, run kuke restart <name> (#983); the daemon's reconcile (P7) applies Compatible OutOfSync diffs in place and recreates on Breaking diffs. kuke run itself never mutates a live cell on any source path.

See kind: CellBlueprint and kind: CellConfig for the full manifest reference.

docs.title: Cleanup with --rm
docs.text:
--rm best-effort deletes the cell after it's no longer needed (any return code). kuke run is daemon-only after #566 — KUKEON_NO_DAEMON=true and --run-path promotion are inert for workload verbs and no longer reach an in-process branch for run, so --rm is always available. Cleanup runs from kukeond's reconcile loop, so latency is bounded by the reconcile interval rather than firing the instant the trigger fires.

Triggers:

  • With -d/--detach: the root container's task exits.
  • In the default attach mode: the attach loop exits because the workload terminated, the peer hung up, or an unrecoverable controller error fired — the CLI then sends KillCell so a long-lived root (e.g. sleep infinity) doesn't pin the cell.
  • A clean ^]^] detach is not a trigger: the cell stays alive so the operator can re-attach later (parity with kuke attach).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Start + attach an existing cell
sudo kuke run my-shell

# Same, detach instead of attaching
sudo kuke run my-shell -d

# Create-or-attach a one-shot cell from a file
sudo kuke run -f hello.yaml

# Create + start + attach a fresh cell from a Blueprint
sudo kuke run --from-blueprint shell --param IMAGE=alpine:latest --param CMD="/bin/sh"

# Same Blueprint, pin a specific cell name
sudo kuke run --from-blueprint shell --name my-shell -d

# Use a parameter file, with one CLI override winning on the same key
sudo kuke run --from-blueprint shell --param-file ./shell.env --param IMAGE=alpine:edge

# Create + start + attach a fresh cell from a daemon-stored CellConfig
sudo kuke run --from-config kukeon-dev --realm kuke-system

# Same Config, with a persisted per-cell env override baked into the CellDoc
sudo kuke run --from-config kukeon-dev-pick-issue --env LABEL=bug -d

# Dispatch a headless run from the same config an attached session uses
sudo kuke run --from-config kukeon-dev --mode headless --param PROMPT="triage the backlog" -d

# Fork an existing cell's recipe into a sibling
sudo kuke run --clone kukeon-dev --name kukeon-dev-debug

# One-shot job that cleans itself up after the workload exits
sudo kuke run --from-blueprint batch --rm

docs.text:

  • kuke attach — attach to an already-running cell

docs.title: kuke screenshot
docs.text:
Print an Attachable container's current screen.

kuke screenshot <cell> [-o text|ansi|json] [flags]

The screen is the grid sbsh's own terminal emulator has rendered from the workload's output: what an attached client would see right now, not the raw redraw escape sequences that kuke log prints. Use it to check what an agent's terminal UI is showing, or whether it is waiting at a prompt, without attaching.

<cell> is a positional argument. --realm, --space, and --stack all default to default. The target is resolved exactly like kuke attach.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description -o, --output text Output format: text, ansi, json --container (auto-pick) Container within the cell (omit to auto-pick the only non-root attachable) --realm default Realm that owns the cell --space default Space that owns the cell --stack default Stack that owns the cell

Plus all global flags.

docs.title: Output formats
docs.text: Format Prints text The plain character grid. Trailing blank columns and rows are dropped; each row ends with a newline. ansi The same grid with SGR foreground/background color sequences, so colors survive. json The full screenshot document below, followed by a newline.

docs.title: JSON schema
docs.text:
-o json is a stable schema: these field names and types are not renamed or removed; new fields may be added, so consumers should ignore unknown ones.

{
  "cols": 80,
  "rows": 24,
  "cursorX": 2,
  "cursorY": 2,
  "cursorVisible": true,
  "altScreen": false,
  "text": "$ echo hi\nhi\n$\n",
  "ansi": "$ echo hi\nhi\n$\n"
}
Field Type Meaning cols, rows int Terminal size in cells cursorX int Cursor column, 0-based cursorY int Cursor row, 0-based cursorVisible bool Whether the program has the cursor shown altScreen bool Whether the program is on the alternate screen (full-screen TUIs) text string Same as -o text ansi string Same as -o ansi

docs.title: Where it works
docs.text:
kukeond connects to the container's sbsh control socket and passes the connection back over the kukeond socket (ConnectContainerTerminal); the screenshot bytes never go through kukeond. So kuke screenshot works from the host and from any cell that has the kukeond socket mounted, without access to /opt/kukeon.

With KUKEON_NO_DAEMON=true (or an explicit --run-path), kuke resolves the target in-process (reading cell state and containerd directly) and dials the socket itself, so it needs root on the host, like the other in-process commands.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: The target must be a running Attachable container. A missing cell, a stopped cell, a container that is not Attachable, or a container whose task is not running fail with the same errors as kuke attach, with a non-zero exit and nothing on stdout.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# What is the cell's terminal showing?
kuke screenshot mycell

# Keep colors
kuke screenshot mycell -o ansi

# Machine-readable, for scripts
kuke screenshot mycell -o json | jq -r .text

# Explicit container in a multi-container cell
kuke screenshot web --container claude

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• kuke write — type into the same terminal
  • kuke attach — interactive terminal
  • kuke log — the raw output stream

docs.title: kuke status
docs.text:
kuke status [--json] [--verbose]

Report kukeon daemon, host, state, and parity health.

Run the consolidated health report that replaces the manual kuke get realms vs kuke get realms --no-daemon diff ritual.

Sections: daemon (socket dialable, round-trip, version), host (containerd, cgroup-v2, CNI plugins), state (orphan sockets, residual containerd namespaces, volume dirs missing group-write), storage (per-realm snapshot / lease / content-blob footprint), parity (every kuke get <kind> agrees daemon-side vs in-process). Each line is OK / WARN / FAIL with a one-line remediation hint when the status is not OK.

Exit code 0 when every check is OK or WARN; non-zero when any line is FAIL. The --json form is the machine-readable shape for CI integration; --verbose surfaces the remediation hint on OK rows too.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --json false emit a JSON document instead of the human-readable table --verbose false print the remediation hint on every row, not just WARN/FAIL

Plus all global flags.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0 — every row is OK, or OK mixed with WARN.
  • non-zero — at least one row is FAIL. The structured report on stdout (text or JSON) is the operator-visible failure marker; the non-zero exit code is the CI-visible one.

The contract is set in cmd/kuke/status/status.go — see the errFailingChecks sentinel and the RunE body that returns it on !report.OK.

docs.title: Human-readable (default)
docs.text:
Each section prints as an uppercased header followed by one row per check, padded so the STATUS column lines up across the whole report. A ↳ <hint> line under a row carries the remediation — printed whenever the row is WARN or FAIL, and on OK rows too when --verbose is set. A bottom-line Status: OK or Status: FAIL mirrors the exit code.

$ kuke status
DAEMON
  socket  OK    unix:///run/kukeon/kukeond.sock (rtt 2ms, version v0.6.0)

HOST
  containerd  OK    /run/containerd/containerd.sock (reachable)
  cgroup-v2   OK    /sys/fs/cgroup (cgroup2 mounted; required controllers delegated)
  cni         OK    /opt/cni/bin (bridge, loopback present)

STATE
  run-dir     OK    /run/kukeon (no orphan sockets)
  namespaces  OK    no residual containerd namespaces

STORAGE
  default      OK    default.kukeon.io (12 snapshots, 49 leases, 24 blobs, 5.0 MiB)
  kuke-system  OK    kuke-system.kukeon.io (157 snapshots, 266 leases, 180 blobs, 700.0 MiB)

PARITY
  realms      OK    daemon view matches in-process view
  spaces      OK    daemon view matches in-process view
  stacks      OK    daemon view matches in-process view
  cells       OK    daemon view matches in-process view
  containers  OK    daemon view matches in-process view
  secrets     OK    daemon view matches in-process view
  blueprints  OK    daemon view matches in-process view
  configs     OK    daemon view matches in-process view

Status: OK

docs.title: JSON (--json)
docs.text:
--json emits the same report as a 2-space-indented JSON document. The status field renders the human label ("OK" / "WARN" / "FAIL") rather than an integer so the wire shape doesn't depend on enum order. The shape is the Report struct in cmd/kuke/status/status.go — a top-level ok bool plus a flat checks array, with each row carrying section, name, status, detail, an optional remediation, and (on storage rows) an optional storage payload (snapshots, leases, blobs, blobsBytes) so CI tooling can alert on accumulation without parsing the human Detail string.

{
  "ok": true,
  "checks": [
    {
      "section": "daemon",
      "name": "socket",
      "status": "OK",
      "detail": "unix:///run/kukeon/kukeond.sock (rtt 2ms, version v0.6.0)"
    },
    {
      "section": "host",
      "name": "containerd",
      "status": "OK",
      "detail": "/run/containerd/containerd.sock (reachable)"
    },
    {
      "section": "storage",
      "name": "default",
      "status": "OK",
      "detail": "default.kukeon.io (12 snapshots, 49 leases, 24 blobs, 5.0 MiB)",
      "storage": {
        "snapshots": 12,
        "leases": 49,
        "blobs": 24,
        "blobsBytes": 5242880
      }
    }
  ]
}

A failing daemon dial yields "status": "FAIL" plus a populated remediation field on the affected row, and "ok": false at the top level.

docs.title: What each section checks
docs.text:
Section What it asserts daemon The kukeond socket dials, an RPC round-trip returns the daemon's build version, and the round-trip latency is recorded. Replaces the original kuke ping proposal. host containerd is reachable on the configured socket; cgroup-v2 is mounted on /sys/fs/cgroup with the controllers kukeon requires delegated (the same controller-set check as kuke doctor cgroups); the CNI binaries are present under /opt/cni/bin. The CNI row is advisory: the kukeond image bundles its own plugins and runs CNI from there, so a host that lacks them while the daemon is reachable reports WARN (not FAIL) — it only FAILs when the plugins are absent and the daemon is unreachable (no plugin set to run CNI at all). kuke init does not lay plugins onto the host. state The run-dir under /run/kukeon has no orphan sockets, and no residual containerd namespaces survive from a half-cleaned kuke uninstall, and every volume dir under <RunPath>/data/**/volumes/<name> keeps group rwx (mode & 0o070 == 0o070; WARN otherwise — non-root cells mounting it lose write access). storage For every realm, the containerd namespace's snapshot count, lease count, and content-blob count plus summed byte size. Surfaces snapshot/lease/content accumulation early so a leak is visible before the data volume hits ENOSPC. Per-snapshot disk usage is intentionally omitted — the figures come from containerd metadata-store iterators (cheap), not an on-disk du (expensive). parity For every resource kind (realm, space, stack, cell, container, secret, blueprint, config), the daemon's view and the in-process controller's view agree. This is the cross-kind generalization of the two-line kuke get realms diff the make dev-init smoke pins.

See CLAUDE.md §"Post-init: kuke status" for the operator narrative that positions this command inside the dev-init smoke loop; this page is the reference.

docs.title: When to use vs kuke doctor cgroups and the realm-parity diff
docs.text: kuke status is the umbrella health command — one invocation covers the daemon, the host pre-flight, run-dir state, and the cross-kind daemon-vs-in-process parity walk. kuke doctor cgroups is a narrower pre-kuke init host check focused on cgroup-v2 controller delegation; kuke status includes the same controller-set assertion in its host section, so once the daemon is up kuke status subsumes kuke doctor cgroups for the cgroup signal specifically. The two-line kuke get realms vs kuke get realms --no-daemon diff make dev-init prints stays the minimal pinned regression guard the smoke test exits on; kuke status is the broader post-kuke init sweep an operator runs to surface anything that two-realm tail won't catch (cgroup delegation gone, CNI binaries gone, divergent secrets/blueprints/configs, residual containerd namespaces from a half-cleaned kuke uninstall).

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• kuke init — bootstrap step kuke status smoke-tests after
  • kuke doctor — the narrower cgroup-only pre-kuke init check
  • kuke get — the per-kind list/describe commands whose daemon-vs-in-process parity the parity section walks

docs.title: kuke team add
docs.text:
kuke team add DIRECTORY [--name NAME] [--source REPOSITORY] [--branch B | --tag T | --commit C] [--host ENDPOINT] [--configuration PATH]
kuke team add NAME --source REPOSITORY [--branch B | --tag T | --commit C] [--host ENDPOINT] [--configuration PATH]

Compose a project team, apply its blueprints and configs to kukeond, and register it under ~/.kuke/kuketeam.d/<name>.yaml. add creates no cells and starts nothing. Run kuke team init first. For the shared composition model, see Teams.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --source — Project Git remote (SCP-style SSH, ssh://, or HTTPS). Required in NAME mode. --branch — Select a branch (default: local HEAD for directories, remote HEAD for named sources). --tag — Select a tag. --commit — Select a full commit object ID (40 or 64 hex characters). --name — Override the team name (default: local Team metadata.name, then the directory basename). --host — kukeond Unix endpoint. Overrides KUKEON_HOST and ClientConfiguration.spec.host. --configuration — kuke ClientConfiguration path. Defaults to KUKE_CONFIGURATION, then ~/.kuke/kuke.yaml.

kuke's global flags (--verbose, --log-level, --run-path, --no-daemon) are accepted but have no effect on kuke team subcommands: they resolve the operator home, the kukeond endpoint and the ClientConfiguration themselves.

--branch, --tag, and --commit are mutually exclusive. Explicit empty --name, --source, or revision flags fail.

docs.title: Adding a named team from a Git source
docs.text:
Register a named team without a local project checkout or Team file:

kuke team add kukeon --source git@github.com:eminwux/kukeon.git
kuke team add kukeon --source ssh://git@work-alias:2222/eminwux/kukeon.git --branch develop
kuke team add kukeon --source https://github.com/eminwux/kukeon.git --tag v1.0.0
kuke team add kukeon --source github.com/eminwux/kukeon --commit <full-commit-object-id>

The positional argument names the team; root and kuke are reserved. Without a selector, native git ls-remote --symref discovers the remote HEAD branch and saves that branch name. A detached or missing remote HEAD requires an explicit selector. Branches remain floating selectors; tags select refs/tags/<name> and commits select the object ID. All selections are fetched and checked out before application, including the project source when it supplies no role/harness definitions. The explicit-source form does not read a local kuketeam.yaml.

docs.title: Adding from a directory
docs.text:
cd /path/to/my-project
kuke team add .
kuke team add . --name my-team
kuke team add ../another-project --source git@host:owner/repo.git --tag v1.0.0

An existing directory argument selects directory mode (including a bare relative name); ./name makes that intent explicit. Otherwise use NAME --source REPOSITORY. Directory mode reads kuketeam.yaml when present, as a strict apiVersion: kuketeams.io/v1, kind: Team declaration. Other kinds, invalid YAML, unknown fields, multiple documents, and unreadable files fail. A missing file starts with an inheriting declaration. The directory and authored file are never modified; uncommitted local content is not uploaded or used for definitions.

Naming precedence is --name, the local metadata.name, then the directory basename. Names use lowercase letters, digits, dots or hyphens, start and end with a letter or digit, and cannot be a reserved name.

For example, kukeon's own kuketeam.yaml composes the kukeon team: roles from the agents repository, harnesses from this repository through the project source:

apiVersion: kuketeams.io/v1
kind: Team
metadata: { name: kukeon }
spec:
  sources:
    - name: agents
      url: git@github.com:eminwux/agents
      branch: main
      clonePath: /home/user/agents
  roles:
    - { name: dev, source: agents, path: dev, needs: { image: [go, root] } }
    - { name: pm, source: agents, path: pm }
    - { name: pr-reviewer, source: agents, path: pr-reviewer }
    - {
        name: pipeline,
        source: agents,
        path: pipeline,
        harness: script,
        tasks: [{ name: tick, suspend: false }],
      }
  harnesses:
    - { name: claude, source: project, path: team/harnesses/claude }
    - { name: codex, source: project, path: team/harnesses/codex }
    - { name: script, source: project, path: team/harnesses/script }

--source overrides only projectSource.url. One of --branch, --tag, or --commit replaces the entire local revision selection. Without overrides, local project-source fields win over discovery. A missing source name becomes project; an omitted clone destination becomes /home/user/<accepted-team-name>. Authored clone destinations are retained.

For an unspecified URL, native Git reads remote.origin.url from the local Git metadata. For an unspecified revision, it records the current local branch, or the full current commit ID for a detached HEAD. Git worktrees are supported. No origin or revision is guessed: missing Git metadata or origin, an unborn HEAD, or an unusable source/revision reports an error with override guidance. The selected revision must be available from the remote; push local-only commits and branches, or override them, before adding.

docs.title: Reserved names
docs.text:
add refuses two team names, whether given positionally, with --name, or as the directory's metadata.name, with an error naming the reserved name before anything is fetched or applied:

  • root — the legacy root identity.
  • kuke — the operator's system team that kuke team init registers at ~/.kuke/kuketeam.d/kuke.yaml. A project team under that name would overwrite its entry and prune its kuke-majordomo-* configs, which carry the same kukeon.io/team: kuke label.

add also refuses a name whose ~/.kuke/kuketeam.d/<name>.yaml is still the init team as registered before its rename to kuke: on a host not yet migrated, adding kukeon fails with run kuke team init --force first, since recording a project on that entry would stop init from migrating it.

Any other name, kukeon included, is a project team: adding kukeon's own checkout leaves kuke.yaml and the kuke-majordomo-* configs untouched.

docs.title: The project source and inherited defaults
docs.text:
Prerequisites are Git, kukeond, and the parent default/default/default realm/space/stack metadata. ~/.kuke/kuketeams.yaml is optional and hand-written: add reads it when it exists, never writes it, and uses empty global defaults without it. It has no spec.git; a file that still has one fails to decode (see kuke team init). add uses the same endpoint and client configuration precedence as kuke team init.

init leaves global defaults empty. Configure reusable sources, roles, and harnesses first (see reusable defaults), or provide explicit selections in the directory's Team declaration. The operator's own selections in kuke.yaml do not become defaults for project teams. Omitted spec.sources, spec.roles, and spec.harnesses inherit global defaults; authored lists replace them, and an explicit [] selects none.

The additional project source is named project, with the clone destination /home/user/<team-name>. It is combined with the resolved definition sources, so inherited roles and harnesses keep their repositories, and roles or harnesses may reference source: project to load definitions from the project itself. Any existing source named project is a preflight error, and duplicate clone destinations fail rather than replacing another checkout.

The accepted TeamEntry stores an additive top-level projectSource, the secret bindings its selected pairs use (see Secrets), and the original omitted/explicit spec selections:

apiVersion: kuketeams.io/v1
kind: TeamEntry
metadata:
  name: kukeon
projectSource:
  name: project
  url: git@github.com:eminwux/kukeon.git
  branch: main
  clonePath: /home/user/kukeon
secrets: # Generated when a selected role needs gh-token; edits are kept.
  - name: gh-token
    secretRef: { name: gh-token, realm: default }
    envName: GH_TOKEN
spec: {}

Omitted fields are not frozen into the entry, so later recomposition inherits the current global defaults. Repeated add replaces the project source and revision, retaining explicit selections in an existing valid registration. It never resets global configuration.

add reads the global role/harness selections, parameters, and scoped secret bindings. It selects published images from each harness's image catalog. It does not build images or create or start cells. Existing runtime secrets are reused; missing ones use an explicit env/file creation source or report a kuke provisioning command.

docs.title: Git transports and host credentials
docs.text:
Supported remote forms are SCP-style [user@]host:path, explicit ssh://[user@]host[:port]/path, HTTPS, and the github.com/owner/repo HTTPS shorthand. SSH URLs stay SSH. Host aliases and custom ports use native Git/SSH settings. git@github.com/owner/repo is malformed: use git@github.com:owner/repo or ssh://git@github.com/owner/repo. Local paths, file://, HTTP, and other schemes are rejected.

Do not put passwords, tokens, query parameters, or fragments in source URLs. HTTPS userinfo is rejected; SSH usernames such as git@ are allowed. Git output and credential-helper output are never included in diagnostics or generated documents.

Discovery and fetch use native Git with the caller's environment and configuration. HTTPS uses configured Git credential helpers; public repositories need none. For SSH, configure hosts, identities, ports, and trusted host keys in your OpenSSH configuration, and load the identity into your agent (ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519) before running add. Git runs non-interactively (BatchMode=yes, no terminal, prompts disabled) with a one-minute deadline per subprocess.

Host-side fetch validates the source for composition only; it does not provision clone credentials for future cells. A cell still needs access to every requested repository, the published image, and its harness/provider authentication. add does not forward the host SSH agent or copy keys.

Inside a cell, repositories are cloned and pushed with stored git credentials: the git connector identity a Realm, Space or Stack default names, or the one the team names under connectors.git. add writes no git defaults. Store yours with kuke connector import git --default (see the git credentials guide). The transport follows the credential, not the URL: a project added by its HTTPS URL is still cloned and pushed over SSH when its host is bound to an SSH key, so an API token in the cell can never take over a push.

When the team clones a source over SSH that states no credential of its own, and neither a scope default nor a Config names a git identity, add prints the note no git identity is set; run kuke connector import git --default.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: Roles declare only requirement names. add binds each required secret for the selected role/harness pairs and records the bindings in the TeamEntry: a binding already recorded there wins, then a global spec.secrets binding, then a generated default (same-named secret in realm default, env var upper-snake cased: gh-token → GH_TOKEN). No global configuration is needed. If a bound runtime secret does not exist and has no source, add still applies and registers the team, exits 0, and prints the kuke create secret … command for each missing one; create them before launching cells. See secret declarations for overrides and kuke team init for creation sources.

docs.title: Registration and recovery
docs.text:
Before mutating the daemon, add validates source references, selected definitions, images, and required secret bindings and scopes, and stages a complete 0600 entry beside ~/.kuke/kuketeam.d/<name>.yaml. It calls ApplyDocumentsForTeam with the team's stable ownership identity and publishes the registration by atomic rename only after full application success. Repeated add converges the same resources and one registration; obsolete team-owned configs are pruned, and a shared blueprint the team stops using is removed once no other CellConfig references it.

Failure returns nonzero and preserves any previous accepted entry. A partial apply or ambiguous RPC failure can leave some daemon resources changed. Fix the prerequisite and rerun the same command, including any explicit revision flags. add does not roll back created secrets or resources, launch cells, or retry ambiguous writes.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Applied 6 resources; registered team kukeon: /home/me/.kuke/kuketeam.d/kukeon.yaml
No cells created or started.

The count is the team's shared blueprints (one per harness × security profile it uses) plus one CellConfig per role/harness pair, plus one headless task CellConfig per role/harness pair × selected role task, plus one when the Realm's secret defaults were written. A pair's config is named <team>-<role>-<harness>, and each of its task configs is named <team>-<role>-<harness>-<task>. See Tasks. Missing runtime secrets and notes are listed after it, as for kuke team init.

docs.title: kuke team init
docs.text:
kuke team init [--force | --reapply] [--host ENDPOINT] [--configuration PATH]

Apply the kuke team, whose one role is majordomo, to kukeond and register it at ~/.kuke/kuketeam.d/kuke.yaml. init creates no cells and starts nothing; launch a composed cell explicitly with kuke afterwards (for example kuke run --from-config kuke-majordomo-codex).

kuke is the operator's system team, named after the kuke- system prefix (cf. the kuke-system realm). The name is reserved: kuke team add refuses it, so a project team — including kukeon's own, which is named kukeon — can never take over its registration or its configs.

To register a project team after init, use kuke team add. For the shared composition model, see Teams.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --force false Replace the registered kuke team with the initial majordomo declaration and apply it. --reapply false Recompose and apply the kuke team from its stored entry. Excludes --force. --host — kukeond Unix endpoint. Overrides KUKEON_HOST and ClientConfiguration.spec.host. --configuration — kuke ClientConfiguration path. Defaults to KUKE_CONFIGURATION, then ~/.kuke/kuke.yaml.

The git identity flags --import-git-identity, --git-key, --git-key-passphrase-file and --git-known-hosts were removed. Init does not read or store a git identity; use kuke connector import git --default (see Git identity and credentials).

kuke's global flags (--verbose, --log-level, --run-path, --no-daemon) are accepted but have no effect on kuke team subcommands: they resolve the operator home, the kukeond endpoint and the ClientConfiguration themselves.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
"Already initialized" means the kuke team entry ~/.kuke/kuketeam.d/kuke.yaml exists. Without --force (or --reapply) init then exits without contacting the daemon:

init: already initialized (/home/me/.kuke/kuketeam.d/kuke.yaml); use --force to reset or --reapply to recompose

kuke team init --force applies the initial kuke team and replaces the entry with the initial majordomo declaration after successful application. It migrates a host initialized while the team was still named kukeon.

~/.kuke/kuketeams.yaml is optional and hand-written. Init reads it when it exists and never writes it, --force included; without it init uses empty global defaults. See reusable defaults.

The command fetches only the sources used by the selected role/harness definitions into temporary Git checkouts, and composes the kuke team's blueprints and configs. Git must be installed and able to read those sources without a terminal prompt. branch, tag, and commit selectors are fetched explicitly; no checkout in the current directory is used. Fetched definitions are removed after the invocation. Runtime repository URLs and clone destinations still come from the authored configuration.

The initial accepted declaration contains the majordomo selections directly. The majordomo role and both harnesses come from the kukeon repository (team/roles/ and team/harnesses/):

apiVersion: kuketeams.io/v1
kind: TeamEntry
metadata:
  name: kuke
spec:
  sources:
    - name: kukeon
      url: github.com/eminwux/kukeon
      branch: main
      clonePath: /home/user/kukeon-src
  roles:
    - name: majordomo
      source: kukeon
      path: team/roles/majordomo
      initialPath: $HOME
      needs:
        image: [go]
  harnesses:
    - name: codex
      source: kukeon
      path: team/harnesses/codex
    - name: claude
      source: kukeon
      path: team/harnesses/claude

This applies the shared blueprints codex and claude — one per harness × security profile, realm-wide, see Teams — and the CellConfigs kuke-majordomo-codex and kuke-majordomo-claude, labelled kukeon.io/team: kuke, that reference them. Init does not start them. The explicit entry keeps recomposition independent of global operator defaults. Configure reusable global defaults separately.

docs.title: Daemon endpoint and client configuration
docs.text:
The command reaches kukeond with the public kukeonv1 Unix JSON-RPC client. Endpoint precedence:

  1. kuke team init --host unix:///absolute/path/to/kukeond.sock
  2. KUKEON_HOST
  3. ClientConfiguration.spec.host
  4. unix:///run/kukeon/kukeond.sock

The configuration path is --configuration, then KUKE_CONFIGURATION, then ~/.kuke/kuke.yaml. An absent default file is allowed; an explicitly selected missing file, an unreadable file, invalid YAML, or a wrong kind/version is an error. Only the Unix transport is accepted. Init does not start the daemon.

Blueprints and configs target the default realm, space, and stack. Preflight checks that the parent metadata exists, checks secret prerequisites, and stages a complete 0600 TeamEntry before mutating the daemon. Provision missing parent scopes with kuke (kuke init creates default/default/default). Init never creates, starts, restarts, or deletes cells. ApplyDocumentsForTeam receives the stable team name kuke, so reruns update that team's resources and prune obsolete team-owned configs. A shared blueprint the team stops using is removed only when no other CellConfig references it. A shared blueprint that already exists with different content is replaced in place, whichever team's configs use it, so every team sees the same content; a note names the old and new content digest and the other configs using it, whose cells turn OutOfSync until kuke restart. Only a blueprint kuke team did not render (no kukeon.io/shared: "true" label) is never overwritten: this team's is applied as <name>-<content digest> instead. A <name>-<content digest> copy an earlier version forked for a shared blueprint is migrated: the team's configs move back to <name>, and the copy is removed, or reported while another config still uses it. It does not prune credentials or running cells.

docs.title: Git identity and credentials
docs.text:
Team cells clone, push and sign with stored git credentials. The host ~/.ssh is never mounted, and init reads nothing from it or from your git configuration. It writes no spec.defaults.git on the team's stack.

A team cell uses the git connector identity a Realm, Space or Stack default names (spec.defaults.git.identityRef), unless the team names one for its Configs (connectors.git.identity). Store yours once and make it the Realm default:

kuke connector import git --default

See kuke connector import git. A source may still state its own identity (sources[].git: author, committer, credential, signing), which is rendered into that repo's fill of each CellConfig.

When the team clones a source over SSH that states no credential of its own, no Realm, Space or Stack default names a git identity, and no Config names its own, init prints one note:

no git identity is set; run kuke connector import git --default

A role's needs.mounts: [ssh] mounts nothing; init prints a note for it.

~/.kuke/kuketeams.yaml has no spec.git. A file that still has one fails to decode:

spec.git: spec.git was removed; store your git identity with kuke connector import git --default (line 4)

Delete the block and run kuke connector import git --default. Nothing is converted: a spec.git block, the stack spec.defaults.git an older init wrote and an older git-ssh secret are left as they are.

Blueprints carry the connector definitions of the kuke build that applied the team. After upgrading kuke, run kuke team init --reapply (or --force) before the team's cells accept an author-only git identity.

docs.title: Authentication and secrets
docs.text:
Only selected role/harness requirements contribute secret lookups. The base majordomo with Codex or Claude does not require gh or gh-token. Selecting OpenCode requires its configured provider binding, as described in secret declarations.

Each runtime secret is identified by all explicit reference coordinates. A successful metadata lookup with MetadataExists: true reuses the existing credential, even when the local creation source is absent, unreadable, or holds a different value. A failed lookup is an error; it never authorizes secret creation.

For a missing secret, init checks the required parent scope and resolves only an explicit source.env variable or source.file path. Missing or empty values fail preflight. File sources follow kuke's trailing-newline removal. All required sources are checked before the first create, and shared runtime identities are created once. Creation happens before dependent blueprints and configs are applied. Credentials and remote secret-error text are never printed or saved in the TeamEntry or the blueprint/config request.

A missing secret without a creation source does not fail init or add. The blueprints/configs are still applied and the team registered (kukeond resolves secret references only when a cell launches), and the command exits 0 after listing each missing runtime secret once:

Missing secrets (cells will not start until they exist):
  provider-account  →  kuke create secret provider-account --realm auth --space shared --stack operators --from-file /path/to/token

Create them before launching cells; no rerun is needed. kuke run still fails on a cell whose secret is absent. The actual command uses the binding's resolved name and scope. A cell-scoped reference requires a Secret manifest with its exact metadata coordinates, applied with kuke apply -f /path/to/secret.yaml.

Init rechecks existence immediately before each create and never retries a secret write, including when a transport failure leaves its outcome ambiguous. On a rerun, a secret accepted by the previous attempt is discovered and reused. Secret rotation is not an init action; rotate explicitly with kuke.

docs.title: Registration and recovery
docs.text: The accepted authored declaration is saved atomically at ~/.kuke/kuketeam.d/kuke.yaml. It retains explicit selections and omitted/empty list semantics, with no resolved credentials or duplicated effective defaults. init --force uses the initial majordomo declaration regardless of an existing kuke.yaml. The name kuke is reserved for this team. Init does not discover or migrate other registrations, apart from the legacy kukeon.yaml below.

docs.title: Reapplying an edited entry
docs.text:
~/.kuke/kuketeam.d/kuke.yaml is the kuke team's editable source. kuke team init --reapply recomposes the team from it, applies the result, and has kukeond prune the team's configs the new composition no longer renders. Use it after editing the entry, for example to turn on the health sweep.

$EDITOR ~/.kuke/kuketeam.d/kuke.yaml
kuke team init --reapply
  • The entry is rewritten only after a fully successful apply, like every registration. A failed apply leaves your edit in place.
  • ~/.kuke/kuketeams.yaml is read when present and never written.
  • The entry is decoded strictly: an unknown or misspelled field, or a task the role does not declare, fails before anything is fetched or applied.
  • Without a stored entry the command fails and tells you to run kuke team init first; it never creates one.
  • --reapply --force is rejected. --force discards the entry and starts again from the initial declaration; --reapply keeps it.
  • --reapply does not import a git identity; nothing in kuke team does. Use kuke connector import git --default.

docs.title: Migrating from the kukeon team name
docs.text:
The init team was named kukeon before it became kuke. That collided with kukeon's own project team (metadata.name: kukeon in the repository's kuketeam.yaml): kuke team add . in a kukeon checkout overwrote the init team's entry and pruned its configs, since both carried kukeon.io/team: kukeon. A host initialized under the old name holds ~/.kuke/kuketeam.d/kukeon.yaml and the configs kukeon-majordomo-codex, kukeon-majordomo-claude and kukeon-majordomo-<harness>-health-sweep.

Run kuke team init --force. When kukeon.yaml is the legacy init declaration — a kukeon entry with no projectSource whose roles are only majordomo (or operator, see below) — init:

  1. applies kuke-majordomo-codex and kuke-majordomo-claude (and their health-sweep configs) labelled kukeon.io/team: kuke,
  2. deletes every config labelled kukeon.io/team: kukeon, and registers ~/.kuke/kuketeam.d/kuke.yaml,
  3. removes kukeon.yaml and prints a note saying so.

Nothing is deleted until the kuke team has passed the daemon preflight and been applied, so a missing stack or an unreadable secret source leaves the kukeon team as it was. The legacy entry is removed only after the kuke team is registered, so a failed run leaves it in place and rerunning --force finishes the migration. Until then, kuke team add refuses the name kukeon. A kukeon.yaml holding any other declaration — a project team registered with kuke team add, or an init entry you added roles to — is left untouched, together with its configs. Like any --force, the migration starts from the initial declaration: re-make edits you had made to kukeon.yaml (an enabled health sweep, for one) in kuke.yaml and run kuke team init --reapply. Cells already created from the old configs are not touched.

Log in to each harness once more afterwards. The state volume that holds the harness login is named after the config (<config>-state), so a kuke-majordomo-* cell starts with a new, empty volume. The old kukeon-majordomo-* volumes are left in place; delete them with kuke delete volume when you no longer need them.

docs.title: Migrating from the operator role
docs.text:
The team's role was named operator before it became majordomo, and its configs were kukeon-operator-codex and kukeon-operator-claude. On a host initialized then, kuke team init --force migrates as above: the legacy entry counts as the init declaration, so the kukeon-operator-* configs (labelled kukeon.io/team: kukeon) are deleted and the kuke-majordomo-* configs applied. The same re-login applies; the old kukeon-operator-* volumes are left in place.

Registration follows full blueprint/config success only. A secret failure, RPC failure, total resource failure, partial apply, prune failure, or incomplete response returns nonzero and leaves any prior TeamEntry unchanged. A first-time failure creates no registration. Successful resources and created secrets are not rolled back: rerun kuke team init --force after fixing the prerequisite to converge the same kuke identity. A registration write failure after application is reported as such and is also recovered by rerunning init --force.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Read configuration: /home/me/.kuke/kuketeams.yaml
Applied 4 resources; registered kuke team: /home/me/.kuke/kuketeam.d/kuke.yaml
No cells created or started.

The Read configuration line is printed only when ~/.kuke/kuketeams.yaml exists.

Missing runtime secrets and notes follow when there are any:

Missing secrets (cells will not start until they exist):
  git-ssh  →  kuke create secret git-ssh --realm default --type ssh-key --from-file /path/to/private-key  (git credential; or --type basic-auth)
  bot-key  →  kuke create secret bot-key --realm default --connector git --type ssh-key --from-file /path/to/private-key --hosts github.com --author 'Name <email>'  (git identity; or --type basic-auth)
Notes:
  role dev: needs.mounts ssh no longer mounts the host ~/.ssh; cells clone, push and sign with stored git credentials

A Secret named as a git identity (spec.connectors.git.identity) is listed with the --connector git form, since a cell renders only with a Secret tagged for the git connector; replace the example host and author with your own. A credential named directly keeps the plain --type ssh-key form.

The resource count is the shared blueprints plus the CellConfigs, plus one when the Realm's secret defaults were written.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
make test runs the injectable-client success/failure/rerun tests and the real Unix JSON-RPC transport tests. A separate check verifies actual daemon storage, reads back blueprints and configs, repeats application, and confirms that cells are unchanged:

KUKETEAMS_INTEGRATION_HOST=unix:///path/to/disposable/kukeond.sock make test-team-integration

Use a disposable kukeond with existing default/default/default scope metadata. The check uses a unique init-check-* team and deletes only its generated blueprints and configs on cleanup.

docs.title: kuke uninstall
docs.text:
Remove all kukeon runtime state from this host.

kuke uninstall [flags]

This is the global counterpart to kuke purge (which is per-resource). It:

  1. Purges every realm with --cascade — drains spaces, stacks, cells, containers and their containerd tasks/containers, and deletes the containerd namespaces created by kukeon.
  2. Removes /run/kukeon/ recursively.
  3. Removes the configured run path (default /opt/kukeon) recursively.
  4. Removes the kukeon system user and group (no-op if absent).

The /usr/local/bin/kuke binary and the kukeond symlink are not removed — uninstalling runtime state is not the same as uninstalling the binary.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --yes, -y false Skip the interactive confirmation prompt (use this in scripts) --server-configuration /etc/kukeon/kukeond.yaml Path to a ServerConfiguration YAML targeting a specific kukeond instance; scopes the suffix-gated namespace enumeration to that instance

Plus all global flags.

docs.title: Targeting a specific instance
docs.text:
kuke uninstall --server-configuration <path> reads the same precedence chain as kuke init and kuke daemon …:

  1. --server-configuration <path> (flag)
  2. KUKEOND_CONFIGURATION environment variable
  3. /etc/kukeon/kukeond.yaml (default file)
  4. Hardcoded defaults (absent file)

The configured containerdNamespaceSuffix scopes the realm-enumeration loop — an uninstall configured for a non-default suffix (e.g. dev.kukeon.io) enumerates only *.dev.kukeon.io namespaces and never touches the default-instance ones. Running sudo kuke uninstall --server-configuration ./kukeond-dev.yaml tears down the dev instance only.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
By default, kuke uninstall asks for interactive confirmation before doing anything. Pass --yes/-y to skip the prompt.

If any realm fails to drop its containerd namespace, steps 2–4 are skipped: tearing out /opt/kukeon while a residual namespace is still pinning overlay mounts on disk would strand the next kuke init with stale containerd state. The report flags every dir/account row as skipped (realm purge failed) so the half-cleaned host is visible without scrolling to the trailing error.

Resolve the realm-purge failure (often: stop the live daemon, remove the residual containerd namespace by hand) and re-run the command.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0 — every step succeeded (or was already in the target state).
  • non-zero — at least one step failed. Check the report for which row was flagged.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Interactive teardown
sudo kuke uninstall

# Scripted teardown
sudo kuke uninstall --yes

docs.title: uninstall vs. daemon reset vs. purge
docs.text: Command Scope kuke daemon reset Only the kukeond cell + /run/kukeon. User-realm data preserved. kuke daemon reset --purge-system The above plus /opt/kukeon/kuke-system. User-realm data preserved. kuke purge realm <r> --cascade A single realm and its subtree. Daemon stays up. kuke uninstall Every realm, every namespace, /run/kukeon, /opt/kukeon, user/group.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• kuke purge — per-resource aggressive cleanup
  • kuke daemon reset — dev-loop reset of just the daemon cell
  • Init and reset — full reset workflows

docs.title: kuke version
docs.text:
Print client and daemon version strings; warn on mismatch.

kuke version [--no-daemon] [--strict]

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
By default, kuke version prints the client version, then queries the daemon for its version and prints that on a second line. If the two strings differ, a warning is emitted on stderr; with --strict, the command also exits non-zero.

$ kuke version
Client: v0.6.0
Daemon: v0.6.0

When the daemon is unreachable (socket missing, daemon down), the second line is replaced by a Warning: daemon unreachable: <err> on stderr; the client-version stdout line still prints and the exit code stays 0. Use --no-daemon to skip the daemon query entirely.

$ kuke version
Client: v0.6.0
Warning: daemon unreachable: dial unix:///run/kukeon/kukeond.sock: connect: no such file or directory

$ kuke version --no-daemon
Client: v0.6.0

For release builds, the version string is the semver tag. For dev builds, it's whatever VERSION was passed at build time (often v0.0.0-dev or empty).

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --no-daemon false Skip the daemon query — print only Client: <ver> --strict false Exit with non-zero status on a client/daemon version mismatch (the warning on stderr is emitted in both modes)

Plus all global flags.

docs.title: Daemon mismatch behavior
docs.text: Warning: version mismatch (client: <c>, daemon: <d>) is emitted on stderr whenever the two version strings differ. Without --strict, the exit code stays 0 (informational warning); with --strict, the exit code is non-zero. Pair --strict with CI guards on host-upgrade workflows where the operator wants a hard fail if kuke and kukeond drift.

docs.title: kuke write
docs.text:
Write bytes into an Attachable container's terminal input, as if typed.

kuke write <cell> [text|-] [--raw] [flags]

<cell> is a positional argument. --realm, --space, and --stack all default to default. The target is resolved exactly like kuke attach.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --raw false Send bytes verbatim; disable caret and \x escape expansion --container (auto-pick) Container within the cell (omit to auto-pick the only non-root attachable) --realm default Realm that owns the cell --space default Space that owns the cell --stack default Stack that owns the cell

Plus all global flags.

docs.title: Input rules
docs.text:
The rules are the same as sb write:

Input Sends ^@ … ^_ Control bytes 0x00–0x1F: ^C interrupt, ^D EOF, ^M Enter (carriage return), ^[ Escape, ^I Tab ^a … ^z Same as ^A … ^Z ^? DEL (0x7F) \xHH The byte HH (two hex digits), e.g. \x5E for a literal ^ \\ A literal backslash anything else Itself
  • Shell escapes such as \n and \t are not interpreted; they are rejected. Use ^M for Enter, \x0A for a line feed, or --raw.
  • No newline is added. To submit a line, end it with an explicit ^M.
  • - reads stdin until EOF. The same expansion applies unless --raw is set.
  • --raw sends the bytes exactly as given.
  • No text, or empty text, is a no-op.

There is no bracketed-paste flag: kuke cannot tell whether the program in the terminal enabled bracketed paste. To send paste markers, include them with --raw.

docs.title: Where it works
docs.text:
kukeond connects to the container's sbsh control socket and passes the connection back over the kukeond socket (ConnectContainerTerminal); the written bytes never go through kukeond. So kuke write works from the host and from any cell that has the kukeond socket mounted, without access to /opt/kukeon.

With KUKEON_NO_DAEMON=true (or an explicit --run-path), kuke resolves the target in-process (reading cell state and containerd directly) and dials the socket itself, so it needs root on the host, like the other in-process commands.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: The target must be a running Attachable container.
